latest.title: Beyond Rational Choice: A Behavioral Game-Theoretic Frameworkfor Consumer Decision-Making
latest.venue: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
latest.abstract: Since Behavioral Economics explains decisions through bounded rationality and mental shortcuts, it is necessary to incorporate strategic interactions into such analyses. This study develops an integrated framework for analyzing irrational purchasing decisions, which includes elements of Behavioral Economics, non-cooperative Game Theory, econometric analysis, and an integrated model of consumer behavior, the Consumer Irrational Utility Model (CIUM). The study employs a quantitative survey of personal care products consumers in the FMCG market, modeling a consumer and a seller as two players in a 2 × 2 non-cooperative game. The game is analyzed using best-response strategies, followed by the derivation of a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium. The results of the game-theoretic model are then tested using Linear Probability Model (LPM) and Weighted Least Squares (WLS) for estimation purposes. The results of the behavioral determinants, validated in the LPM and WLS estimations, are then incorporated into CIUM, which explains how irrational behavior by a consumer deviates from the utility-maximizing behavior of a rational human being. The study reveals that in the Indian FMCG market, consumers mainly adopt the Relative Decision Paradox strategy, whereas sellers mainly adopt the Strategized Pricing strategy. The study further reveals that the behavioral variables identified in the study have a significant impact on consumers' purchasing decisions. Also, results from the CIUM indicate that the economic utility of a product and the utility influenced by various behavioral factors in strategic interactions in the market jointly determine the overall utility of a product for a consumer.

latest.title: Digital and social media marketing: a bibliometric mapping from 2020 to 2025
latest.abstract: Abstract Digital and social media marketing is reshaping how firms communicate with consumers, gather market intelligence, manage customer journeys, and build brand relationships. This study followed the PRISMA framework to select relevant Scopus-indexed articles between 2020 and 2025 under the business, management, and accounting subject area, using the search terms “digital marketing” and “social media marketing” in titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search, conducted on 20 February 2026 and restricted to open-access, English-language, final-stage journal articles, yielded 1,054 articles. Performance analysis, citation analysis, author-keyword co-occurrence mapping, an average-publication-year overlay, co-citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling were conducted using VOSviewer. Findings reveal publication growth, particularly during 2024 and 2025. Indonesia was the leading country by publications, whereas the UK was the most influential country by citations. Additionally, the “Journal of Business Research” is the most influential, while “Cogent Business & Management” is the most productive journal; the most-cited document is “Setting the future of digital and social media marketing research: Perspectives and research propositions,” with 1,806 citations, produced by “International Journal of Information Management.” Four of the ten prominent authors published six papers each, including Saura, J.R., and Huertas-Garcia, R., both affiliated with Spanish institutions. Keyword mapping identifies digital marketing, social media marketing, social media, consumer behavior, marketing, and purchase intention as central themes. latest.title: Adaptive Decision-Making in Action: Decision-Maker Profiles Under Time Pressure and Incomplete Information
latest.venue: Journal of Intelligence Studies in Business
latest.abstract: Competitive intelligence increasingly requires decision-makers to extract actionable signals from abundant, incomplete, and rapidly changing information within compressed timeframes. Although decision research has extensively examined analytical and intuitive reasoning, less is known about how these modes combine into distinct person-level configurations. Using survey data from 246 employees and a person-centred analytical approach, K-means clustering based on Analytical Orientation, Intuitive Orientation, and Contextual Adaptability identified four distinct profiles: an Analysis-Dominant Profile, an Intuition-Dominant Profile, a Context-Adaptive Profile, and an Analytical–Intuitive Integrative Profile. External validation revealed a significant Profile × Analytical Burden interaction, LR χ²(3) = 29.00, p < .001, indicating that the association between Analytical Burden and negative responses to time pressure differed across profiles. The study develops the concept of Adaptive Decision-Making in Action, defined as the capability to maintain, switch, substitute, or integrate analytical and intuitive reasoning according to situational demands. The findings extend CI research beyond the analytical-intuitive dichotomy by showing that decision-making may take distinct configurational forms and suggest that decision development should focus on the adaptive use of decision modes rather than on a single preferred style.

latest.title: From others to the self: Influence mechanisms of multiple social agents on sustainable consumption
latest.abstract: 摘要： 可持续消费研究长期聚焦个体消费者的心理与行为机制, 无力弥合可持续态度与实际消费行为之间的显著差距。理论演进的脉络梳理表明, 可持续消费的个体选择会受到消费者社会关系网络中多元社会主体的复杂影响。本文系统梳理个体、群体和组织层面的社会主体对消费者可持续消费的影响, 并基于自我决定理论提出了以基本心理需求和动机内化连续体为核心的社会主体影响机制与效应框架。未来研究应重点探讨如何完善多元主体对个体可持续消费的影响机制框架、拓展社会主体的研究边界、推动可持续消费的集体行动研究转向, 从而为破解可持续消费知易行难的现实困境拓展理论空间与实践路径。

latest.title: What shared responses reveal about audience behavior: neural prediction and the emerging potential of peripheral synchrony
latest.abstract: Predicting audience responses to dynamic media remains a significant challenge in neuromarketing and neuroforecasting. Intersubject correlation (ISC) has been proposed to address this need by quantifying the temporal similarity of neural, physiological, and behavioral responses among individuals exposed to the same stimulus. This narrative mini-review examines how ISC relates to preferences, judgments, and behavior and proposes a conceptual framework for interpreting its predictive value. Across modalities, ISC consistently reflects shared stimulus processing and is associated with attention, alongside additional links to engagement, memory, and higher-order narrative processing. Neural ISC has shown associations with individual, group, and population-level outcomes, although findings vary by neural modality, analytic approach, and behavioral endpoint. Peripheral ISC derived from gaze, heart rate, electrodermal activity, and facial expressions provides complementary information about interindividual alignment, but direct evidence for predicting consumer outcomes remains limited. At the same time, neural and peripheral measures capture various aspects of shared response dynamics, and combining them in a multimodal ISC approach may help distinguish synchronization in different functional domains, including perceptual, attentional, autonomic, affective, and valuation-related processes, and clarify their relationship to the target outcome. The proposed framework therefore conceptualizes ISC as a probabilistic predictor whose predictive value depends on which functional processes underlie the observed synchrony and their relevance to the specific outcome of interest.

latest.title: When does controversy discourse correspond to visitor demand? Discursive political consumerism in cultural tourism
latest.abstract: Online controversy discourse around cultural institutions is increasingly visible, yet whether such discourse corresponds to measurable variation in visitor demand remains unclear. This study examines how controversy-discourse frames correspond to visitor demand at the British Museum across two sustained controversies that differ in the degree and locus of institutional actionability: fossil-fuel sponsorship and contested cultural artefacts. Drawing on discursive political consumerism and the moral economy of visiting, we construct engagement-weighted controversy-discourse signals from 2.14 million posts across six major London cultural institutions and link them to weekly British Museum arrivals and monthly attendance for all six institutions. A monthly fixed-effects panel provides the main estimates, complemented by supplementary weekly analyses. At the British Museum, fossil-fuel sponsorship discourse is positively associated with aggregate institutional attendance, whereas contested-artefact discourse is negatively associated but more specification-sensitive. Because the two signals overlap, the frame-specific interpretation remains tentative. Weekly models do not detect a robust short-run arrivals response. The study advances political-consumerism research in cultural tourism by providing a human-validated, frame-differentiated account of associations between public controversy discourse and aggregate institutional attendance. For heritage managers, the findings support assessing controversy discourse alongside attendance, visitor feedback and the institution’s capacity to address sponsorship or restitution claims.

latest.title: How recommendation explanation cues shape consumers’ multistage online behavior: An integrative information-processing framework
latest.abstract: 摘要： 算法推荐已成为电商平台影响消费者决策的重要信息环境, 但既有研究侧重算法类型、准确性及转化效果, 较少考察推荐解释线索对消费者信息加工与多阶段决策的影响。本文聚焦前端的相似用户型与产品属性型解释线索, 将其视为具有不同心理含义的信息线索, 而非后台算法类型: 前者强调相似他人行为, 后者强调产品属性匹配, 并构建购前搜索—购中选择—购后反馈框架。购前, 产品属性型线索通过降低感知产品差异促进目标导向型搜索; 相似用户型线索通过提高感知产品差异促进探索型搜索。购中, 相似用户型线索借助社会证明降低感知产品不确定性, 提高选择不熟悉产品的可能性, 增强选择信心并提升决策效率。购后, 相似用户型线索形成的推荐来源表征通过增强产品社会联结感, 提高反馈努力与质量, 并可能在后续评价触点中被重新激活。本文揭示推荐解释线索通过差异化信息加工机制影响消费者在线多阶段行为, 为推荐解释设计与消费者信息加工研究提供整合框架。

latest.title: Pengaruh Social Media Marketing terhadap Purchase Intention dengan Brand Image dan Brand Awareness sebagai Mediasi pada Produk Kosmetik Hanasui
latest.venue: CEMERLANG Jurnal Manajemen dan Ekonomi Bisnis
latest.abstract: The rapid digitalization of the cosmetics industry has significantly shifted the shopping behavior of Generation Z, making TikTok a highly strategic social media marketing platform. This research aims to examine the impact of social media marketing on purchase intention for Hanasui cosmetic products in Tangerang Regency, incorporating brand image and brand awareness as mediating variables. Employing a quantitative explanatory approach, data were collected through purposive sampling from 110 active TikTok users aged 17 to 27 years old. The empirical data were then analyzed using the Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method via SmartPLS software. The findings reveal that social media marketing has a positive and significant direct effect on brand image, brand awareness, and purchase intention. Furthermore, both brand image and brand awareness positively influence purchase intention and serve as significant mediators in the relationship between social media marketing and purchase intention. Practically, this study suggests that cosmetics companies should develop interactive and engaging digital content to strengthen brand familiarity and positive impressions, which effectively stimulates consumers' purchase intentions.

latest.title: Green nudges for sustainable e-commerce: a bibliometric analysis
latest.abstract: In view of the rising online consumption and growing environmental concerns, e-commerce platforms face a critical dilemma. They need to influence consumer choices toward sustainability without compromising user autonomy or crossing ethical boundaries. Incorporating green nudges—subtle design prompts intended to steer users toward more eco-friendly decisions—has emerged as a promising yet controversial strategy. This study conducts a systematic literature review, following PRISMA guidelines, to examine how green nudges are used in digital commerce and how effective they are in promoting sustainable purchasing patterns. A comprehensive Scopus search of studies on green nudging in e-commerce reveals a 28.21% annual publication growth rate and an average of 25.68 citations across 33 countries. Bibliometric and content analysis reveals emerging themes and identifies the contextual factors that shape the success of these interventions. The findings highlight the potential of green nudges but also reveal key challenges, including inconsistent implementation, culturally variable outcomes, and ethical concerns about manipulation. The review underscores the need for a more nuanced, context-sensitive approach to green nudge design, accounting for user demographics, digital architecture, and behavioral science. This work both synthesizes current knowledge and proposes a research agenda to guide ethical and effective use of green nudges in sustainable e-commerce.

latest.title: Attitudes, Emotions, and Socially Responsible Identity Among Generation Z Consumers in Mexico City
latest.abstract: To analyze the relationship between attitudes, emotions, and socially responsible identity among Generation Z consumers living in Mexico City, considering the mediating role of emotions in responsible food consumption. The study employed a cross-sectional design with 514 young participants from Generation Z. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire based on previously validated instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was applied to analyze the data. The findings revealed that favorable attitudes toward socially responsible food consumption were significantly associated with emotions and with the development of a socially responsible identity. In addition, emotions statistically mediated the association between attitudes and identity. The results underscore the importance of understanding the role of emotional factors in consumer decision-making within the framework of socially responsible identity among Generation Z consumers. The study presents limitations related to its cross-sectional design and the geographic scope of the sample, which was limited to participants from Mexico City. These findings underscore the importance of furthering the debate on the relationships among the study variables in other Mexican contexts and emerging economies.

latest.title: Looking into the Gap: The Mediating Role of Perceived Control and Intrinsic Norms Between Concern for the Future and Responsible Consumption Intentions
latest.abstract: In the pursuit of socially and environmentally conscious consumer behavior, the core challenge lies not just in identifying motivations, but in explaining how core values, intrinsic norms, and attitudes translate into actual intentions. This dynamic is particularly pronounced in Latin America, where socioeconomic constraints and weak regulations on responsible products actively challenge a consumer’s sense of moral obligation and perceived behavioral control. To decode this complexity, this paper applies Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to a sample of 643 consumers in Argentina, examining how environmental and social concerns intersect with intrinsic norms and perceived control to shape responsible purchasing intentions. Empirical findings reveal that environmental and social concerns do not directly drive purchasing intentions, rather, their influence operates through a competitive mediation pattern powered by intrinsic norms and perceived control. This demonstrates that concerns remain latent unless activated by personal agency and internalized moral obligations to guide sustainable choices. This research bridges the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Value-Belief-Norm (VBN) theory, offering vital theoretical insights into how altruistic values, moral norms, and cognitive control efforts intersect in consumer decision-making. By highlighting these critical mediating pathways, this study provides a deeper look into consumer psychology, capturing the sophisticated sensemaking and adaptive agency consumers deploy when navigating adverse market conditions.

latest.title: Examining the Effect of Influencer Credibility and Social Media Exposure on Consumer Buying Behaviour: The Mediating role of Consumer Trust towards Cosmetic Products
latest.venue: WSEAS Transactions on Information Science and Applications archive
latest.abstract: The expansion of social media has transformed the way consumers acquire product information and make purchasing decisions. The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of Influencer credibility and Social media exposure on Consumer buying behaviour, with mediating role of Consumer trust towards Cosmetic products. Primary data were obtained through a structured online questionnaire from 350 consumers in Chennai city, India, who had prior experience in purchasing cosmetic products online. A Purposive sampling technique was employed to select respondents based on predefined eligibility criteria. The obtained data were analysed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to assess the measurement and structural models and test the proposed relationships among the study constructs. latest.title: Generative AI in Consumer Decision Making: How Algorithmic Recommendations Shape Brand Trust
latest.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly moving from the back end of recommendation engines to the consumer-facing interface, where conversational assistants, generated product descriptions and personalised feeds increasingly decide what shoppers see, compare and buy. While the literature on algorithm aversion and algorithm appreciation explains when consumers accept algorithmic advice, little is known about how such advice reshapes trust in the brand that deploys it. This paper develops and specifies a multi-level, testable framework in which four attributes of a GenAI recommendation (perceived personalisation, perceived accuracy and relevance, transparency and explainability, and disclosure of the AI source) influence brand trust through two opposing appraisal pathways: perceived algorithmic competence and fairness, which build trust, and perceived manipulation and privacy concern, which erode it. Brand trust in turn drives purchase intention and loyalty, with AI literacy and task type (utilitarian versus hedonic) as boundary conditions. Nine hypotheses are derived from trust theory, the persuasion knowledge model and the human–automation literature, and a dynamic trust-calibration loop is proposed in which each decision cycle updates the trust baseline used in the next. A two-study empirical design is specified, comprising a PLS-SEM survey and a 3 × 2 × 2 online experiment, and a Monte Carlo power analysis shows that a survey of about 300 respondents gives at least 95% power for the main hypothesised paths, while a 600-participant experiment gives about 92% power for medium-small effects of disclosure. latest.title: The Influence of Social Media Marketing and Brand Awareness on Purchase Decisions for Decoration Services at Catasa.id In South Tangerang
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of Social Media Marketing and Brand Awareness on purchase decisions for decoration services through Instagram @Catasa.id, both partially and simultaneously. The research used a quantitative associative approach. Data were collected through questionnaires from 106 respondents who knew or had interacted with @Catasa.id. The data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, simple and multiple linear regression, correlation, coefficient of determination, t-test, and F-test with IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The results show that Social Media Marketing has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (t = 8.361; p < 0.001), while Brand Awareness has a positive but insignificant effect (t = 0.925; p = 0.357). Simultaneously, Social Media Marketing and Brand Awareness have a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (F = 70.849; p < 0.001). The coefficient of determination is R² = 0.579, indicating that 57.9% of the variation in purchase decisions is explained jointly by the two independent variables.

latest.title: AFETO PARA UNS, PRATICIDADE PARA OUTROS: A PARTICIPAÇÃO DOS ASPECTOS AFETIVOS NA ESCOLHA DE INSTITUIÇÕES FINANCEIRAS
latest.abstract: Com a digitalização dos serviços financeiros, bancos tradicionais, cooperativas de crédito e fintechs ficaram mais parecidos, e aspectos afetivos ganharam espaço na escolha do consumidor. Este estudo analisou de que forma esses aspectos participam da escolha de instituições financeiras e se essa participação é semelhante entre os consumidores. Foi realizado um survey com 291 consumidores de Foz do Iguaçu-PR, que avaliaram oito afirmações em escala Likert de cinco pontos, analisadas por estatística descritiva, tabulação cruzada e teste qui-quadrado. O afeto apareceu no momento da escolha, pela experiência pessoal e pelo sentimento em relação à instituição, e na relação com ela, pelo vínculo, pela disposição para defendê-la e pelo sentimento de ser valorizado. A praticidade se comportou como critério oposto ao afeto, pois quem a priorizou se afastou das afirmações afetivas. Conclui-se que o afeto participa da decisão, mas não da mesma forma para todos, o que sugere perfis distintos de consumidores.

latest.title: Structural insights into the effects of generative AI-empowered social media marketing on customer-brand engagement and purchase behaviors: evidence from China's platform economy
latest.abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities in enhancing customer purchase intentions through the mediating roles of brand equity and relationship equity within China’s platform economy. As generative artificial intelligence increasingly transforms digital interactions between brands and consumers, understanding its influence on customer engagement and purchasing behavior has become increasingly important. Data were collected from 620 Chinese consumers and analyzed using structural equation modeling to examine the relationships among generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities, customer–brand engagement, brand equity, relationship equity, and purchase intention. The findings reveal that generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities exert significant positive effects on customer–brand engagement, purchase intention, brand equity, and relationship equity. Brand equity significantly enhances both customer–brand engagement and purchase intention, confirming its important role in converting artificial intelligence-enabled social media marketing efforts into favorable consumer outcomes. Relationship equity significantly influences purchase intention but does not significantly affect customer–brand engagement. Furthermore, customer–brand engagement does not significantly influence purchase intention. The mediation results indicate that brand equity significantly mediates the effects of generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities on both customer–brand engagement and purchase intention. latest.title: Transparency that sells: the impact of anti–pre-made dishes attitude disclosure on restaurant patronage intentions
latest.abstract: Introduction Although industrially produced pre-made (PMDs) offer convenience, their use in restaurants may conflict with consumers’ expectations of freshness and culinary craftsmanship. Drawing on signaling theory and expectancy violation theory, this study examines how restaurants’ disclosure of an anti-PMD stance influences patronage dishes through perceived moral authenticity and perceived risk, and whether these effects depend on operational transparency. Methods Four between-subjects scenario experiments were conducted in casual-restaurant contexts involving offline dining and online food delivery. Two single-factor experiments examined the effects of anti-PMD disclosure (presence versus absence), while two 2 × 2 factorial experiments further manipulated operational transparency (closed versus open kitchens). The hypotheses were tested using analysis of variance, bootstrap mediation analysis, and moderated mediation analysis. Results Anti-PMD disclosure increased patronage intention and perceived moral authenticity while reducing perceived food-related risk. Perceived moral authenticity and perceived risk mediated the relationship between disclosure and patronage intention. Operational transparency moderated these relationships: disclosure significantly influenced patronage intention and both mediators in closed-kitchen settings, whereas these effects were not significant in open-kitchen settings. The indirect effects through both mediators were also significant in closed-kitchen settings but not in open-kitchen settings. Discussion These findings clarify how food-preparation information and operational transparency jointly shape the psychological evaluations underlying consumers’ food-provider choice intentions. latest.title: Jarak Budaya sebagai Filter Kontekstual dalam Perilaku Konsumen Digital Internasional: Tinjauan Integratif dan Agenda Riset untuk Strategi Pemasaran Digital
latest.venue: Bisman (Bisnis dan Manajemen) The Journal of Business and Management
latest.abstract: Digital marketing increasingly reaches consumers across national borders, yet evidence on whether cultural distance weakens or strengthens the effectiveness of digital strategies remains fragmented. This study synthesizes recent and foundational research on digital consumer behavior in international markets and clarifies the moderating role of cultural distance in digital marketing strategies. An integrative literature review was conducted with targeted searches for peer-reviewed studies published between 2021 and 2026. 51 sources were coded into six themes: distance measurement, trust and perceived risk, privacy and disclosure, platform-specific engagement, localization versus standardization, and specific cultural moderators. The synthesis indicates that cultural distance operates as a contextual filter rather than a uniform main effect. It conditions how consumers interpret trust cues, privacy assurances, social proof, and message style, and its apparent influence depends strongly on how distance is measured. Selective adaptation is the best-supported strategy: localizing language, payment and logistics communication, privacy assurances, and culturally salient appeals, while standardizing familiar brand assets. The article proposes an integrative framework and six testable propositions, and recommends multi-measure, invariance-tested, multilevel designs for future research.

latest.title: Neuromarketing y estrategias de comunicación para pymes: revisión de alcance con síntesis neutrosófica (T, I, F) de la evidencia
latest.abstract: Las pymes necesitan saber qué estrategias de comunicación tienen respaldo en la investigación de neuromarketing, pero la literatura mezcla estudios de calidad y alcance muy distintos. Esta revisión de alcance, informada según PRISMA 2020 y su extensión para revisiones de alcance, buscó en OpenAlex artículos de 2010 a 2026 que midieran con técnicas neurofisiológicas o biométricas la respuesta del consumidor a seis estrategias: narrativa emocional, prueba social, diseño sensorial, escasez y urgencia, personalización e influenciadores. De 975 registros se incluyeron 150 estudios; el 74 % usó seguimiento ocular y solo 5 se realizaron con pymes o para ellas. La evidencia de cada estrategia se resumió en una tripleta neutrosófica (T, I, F) calculada, no asignada: T y F son cotas inferiores de Clopper-Pearson de las proporciones de estudios con efecto favorable y con efecto nulo o desfavorable, e I se separa en resultados mixtos y escasez de estudios. Solo el diseño sensorial obtuvo un veredicto de apoyo (T = 0,59, n = 83). La narrativa emocional quedó indecisa por falta de estudios (T = 0,32), y prueba social, escasez, personalización e influenciadores quedaron indecisas porque sus resultados dependen de la condición. No se certificó contradicción entre medidas implícitas y declaradas. Para las pymes, I es casi total: ninguna estrategia reúne más de 3 estudios en ese contexto. Una ordenación orientativa con TOPSIS y VIKOR, construida solo con criterios derivados de la evidencia, sitúa diseño sensorial y narrativa emocional en los dos primeros lugares y la personalización en el último, por su mayor riesgo ético documentado y su escasa evidencia.

latest.title: Towards Sufficiency in Consumer Electronics? Consumers’ Perceptions of Longevity Strategies for Postponing Product Replacement
latest.abstract: The circular economy highlights the need to slow resource use by making products last longer. Although various longevity strategies have been proposed, it remains unclear whether consumers perceive these strategies as effective. This paper draws on literature on lifetime extension strategies and behavioural theories to investigate the extent to which consumers perceive these strategies as effective in postponing replacement. A survey of 617 consumers examined the perceived effectiveness of 13 product lifetime extension strategies across four product categories using ANOVAs. Durability and reliability emerged as the strategies perceived to be most effective. Preventing functional problems during product use is particularly important for postponing product replacement, as such problems appear to be prominent triggers for replacement. However, consumers remain unconvinced about the effectiveness of most other strategies. Correlational analyses revealed that satisfaction with lifetimes is negatively correlated with perceived strategy effectiveness, suggesting that consumers are less likely to search for lifetime-extending strategies as they do not see lifetime as a concern. These findings underscore the need for design/policy interventions to strengthen durability and enhance awareness of lifetime-extending strategies.

latest.title: Strategi Rebranding Bakpia Djava (Repositioning, Redesign, Relaunching) Dalam Mempertahankan Daya Saing Produk Oleh-Oleh Tradisional
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis strategi rebranding Bakpia Djava dan kontribusinya dalam mempertahankan daya saing sebagai produk oleh-oleh tradisional Yogyakarta. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan wawancara mendalam terhadap Head Marketing dan Konsultan F&B Bakpia Djava, penelitian ini mengkaji fenomena rebranding yang dilakukan pada Juni 2025. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rebranding didorong oleh tekanan persaingan pasar dan perubahan perilaku konsumen generasi muda di era digital. Implementasi mencakup perubahan logo menjadi lebih humanis, pergantian tagline dari "Resep Tradisional Tempo Doeloe" menjadi "Cita Rasa Tempo Doeloe", serta peluncuran tiga kategori kemasan berdasarkan strata sosial konsumen. Dampak rebranding terlihat pada peningkatan kunjungan, omset penjualan, dan penguatan keunggulan merek melalui strategi pembuktian kualitas produk. Keunikan strategi Bakpia Djava terletak pada penerapan kolaborasi kompetitif dengan kompetitor dan manajemen transisi visual yang mempertahankan logo lama untuk menjaga loyalitas pelanggan setia. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa rebranding yang memadukan pembaruan identitas visual dengan pelestarian nilai tradisional dan strategi kolaboratif efektif dalam mempertahankan daya saing produk oleh-oleh tradisional di era digital

latest.title: Examining the role of digital promotion, referral, and CRM in shaping decisions to enroll in RPL programs
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Bisnis dan Ekonomi Asia
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of digital promotion, referral, and customer relationship management (CRM) on study decisions in the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) program at Institut Teknologi dan Bisnis ASIA Malang. A quantitative approach was employed to analyze the partial and simultaneous effects of the independent variables on prospective students’ decisions to choose the RPL program. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to respondents associated with the RPL program and analyzed using appropriate statistical techniques. The results indicate that digital promotion has a positive and significant effect on study decisions, suggesting that accessible digital information, engaging promotional content, and clear communication can strengthen prospective students’ interest and confidence. Referral also has a positive and significant effect, indicating that recommendations from alumni, current students, family members, and colleagues can enhance trust in the RPL program. Furthermore, CRM has a positive and significant effect on study decisions, particularly through effective information services, prompt communication, consultation accessibility, and responsiveness to prospective students’ needs. These findings highlight the importance of integrating digital promotion, referral strategies, and relationship-based services to strengthen enrollment decisions in RPL programs.

latest.title: Building Trust for Second-Hand Purchase on P2P Resale Platforms: Interactive Effect of Seller-Generated Content and Relationship Norms
latest.abstract: Second-hand consumption on peer-to-peer (P2P) online platforms, as a form of extended product use, is often associated with circular economy initiatives. Yet consumer participation in these markets remains constrained by uncertainty and a lack of trust in sellers. While seller-generated content (SGC) can help build consumer trust, the specific psychological mechanisms through which different SGC types promote second-hand purchase intention remain underexplored. Drawing on relationship norms theory and signaling theory, this study differentiates competence-based trust from benevolence-based trust and explores how the interplay between SGC types and relationship norms facilitates consumers’ second-hand purchase intention via distinct trust pathways. Through three experiments, we demonstrate that seller-generated content (informational vs. emotional) and relationship norms (exchange vs. communal) interact to influence consumers’ second-hand purchase intention. Specifically, informational seller-generated content is more effective under exchange relationship norms in fostering competence-based trust and promoting purchase intention, whereas emotional seller-generated content is more effective under communal relationship norms in strengthening benevolence-based trust and driving purchase intention. These findings contribute to research on trust formation and consumer decision-making in P2P resale markets and offer practical implications for designing norm-congruent seller communication on second-hand platforms.

latest.title: Balancing budgets and emotions: The dual influence of economic and psychological factors on furniture purchase decisions during relocation
latest.abstract: Furniture purchasing is a high-involvement consumer decision, particularly during relocation, when consumers must navigate both financial and psychological considerations. Despite extensive research on consumer behaviour, limited attention has been given to how these factors jointly shape furniture purchase decisions during relocation, particularly in the Malaysian context. This exploratory study employed a quantitative research design to examine the influence of economic and psychological factors on furniture purchase decisions before relocation. Data were collected from 218 adult consumers through a structured online questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The findings show that both economic and psychological factors significantly influence consumer purchase decisions, with psychological factors emerging as the stronger predictor. This suggests that, alongside financial considerations, consumers place considerable importance on comfort, personal preferences, lifestyle compatibility, and adjustment to their new living environment. The findings extend the application of the Theory of Reasoned Action and the Theory of Planned Behaviour to relocation-related consumer behaviour and contribute to a better understanding of high-involvement purchasing during significant life transitions. Practically, the findings suggest that furniture retailers and marketers should combine affordability and flexible purchasing options with strategies that address consumers’ psychological and lifestyle needs.

latest.title: Examining the role of artificial intelligence and social media marketing activities through the brand resonance model
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractIn an era where digital technologies are rapidly transforming consumer behavior, e-commerce platforms have emerged as primary channels for purchasing goods. This shift has prompted organizations to adapt their marketing strategies to increasingly competitive digital environments, particularly by applying artificial intelligence and social media to build consumer relationships and strengthen customer-based brand equity. This study aims to examine the effects of Artificial Intelligence Marketing Activities (AIMA) and Social Media Marketing Activities (SMMA) on brand resonance, using Keller’s brand resonance model as the main theoretical framework. Data were collected through an online survey from 210 respondents in Thailand and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that both AIMA and SMMA have significant positive effects on brand salience, brand performance, and brand imagery. These constructs subsequently influence brand judgments and feelings, ultimately leading to brand resonance. The findings extend the application of the brand resonance model to the digital marketing context, contribute to a deeper understanding of how AI-driven and social media marketing can be effectively managed on digital platforms, and provide practical implications for developing marketing strategies aimed at strengthening brand equity.AcknowledgementsThe authors would like to thank all participants for their contribution to this study.

latest.title: Which review cues matter most? Perceived authenticity as the dominant predictor of purchase intention toward Indonesian local fashion brands
latest.abstract: In digital fashion markets, consumers navigate a complex landscape of online reviews, although the cues they prioritize when evaluating local brands remain poorly understood. Grounded in signalling theory and the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM), this study develops a multi-cue framework examining how review content quality, review source credibility, perceived review authenticity, and emotional tone collectively predict purchase intention toward local fashion brands. Drawing on survey data from Generation Z consumers in Indonesia analyzed through PLS-SEM, the findings reveal a signal hierarchy: perceived review authenticity consistently emerges as the dominant evaluative cue, outweighing informational and credibility-based signals alike. This pattern suggests that consumers in identity-driven consumption contexts prioritize legitimacy verification above argument evaluation, a finding that departs from prior ELM-based review research in which argument quality typically dominates. Theoretically, the study contributes to signalling theory by suggesting that signal effectiveness depends on imitation cost relative to the prevailing manipulation environment and identifies a scope condition for ELM in contexts where message authenticity cannot be presumed. Practically, local fashion brands are advised to cultivate authentic consumer narratives rather than optimizing review volume or aggregate ratings.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kredibilitas Influencer Dan Kualitas Konten Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Produk Somethinc Pada Generasi Z Di Kota Bandung
latest.abstract: Perkembangan industri skincare di Indonesia tidak terlepas dari perubahan perilaku konsumen dalam mencari dan mengevaluasi informasi produk melalui influencer dan konten media sosial. Meskipun demikian, bukti empiris mengenai pengaruh kedua faktor tersebut terhadap keputusan pembelian produk skincare lokal, khususnya pada Generasi Z, masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kredibilitas influencer dan kualitas konten terhadap keputusan pembelian produk Somethinc pada Generasi Z di Kota Bandung. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain asosiatif. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 126 responden yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Data dianalisis menggunakan analisis regresi linear berganda dengan bantuan IBM SPSS Statistics Versi 27. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kredibilitas influencer (β = 0,568; p < 0,05) dan kualitas konten (β = 0,356; p < 0,05) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Secara simultan, kedua variabel juga berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian (F = 186,847; p < 0,05) dengan koefisien determinasi sebesar 0,752, yang menunjukkan bahwa 75,2% variasi keputusan pembelian dapat dijelaskan oleh kedua variabel tersebut. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kredibilitas influencer merupakan faktor yang lebih dominan dibandingkan kualitas konten dalam memengaruhi keputusan pembelian. Penelitian ini memperkuat penerapan Source Credibility Theory dalam konteks pemasaran digital serta memberikan bukti empiris bahwa pemilihan influencer yang kredibel dan penyajian konten yang berkualitas merupakan strategi yang efektif dalam meningkatkan keputusan pembelian produk Somethinc pada Generasi Z di Kota Bandung

latest.title: Attention Economy and Marketing Mechanisms: A Comparison of Low- and High-Involvement Products
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: In the era of the attention economy, consumer attention has become an increasingly scarce and valuable marketing resource. With the rapid development of digital platforms and algorithmic recommendation technologies, the way firms acquire and utilize consumer attention has undergone significant changes. This paper uses a conceptual analysis examines how attention-based marketing mechanisms differ across products with different levels of consumer involvement. By integrating insights from attention-based marketing theory and consumer decision-making literature, this paper analyzes two distinct pathways through which attention is transformed into purchase behavior: low-involvement products primarily rely on attention repetition and mental availability to stimulate purchasing, while high-involvement products require deeper information processing and trust formation after attention is captured. The study further discusses how firms can allocate attention resources effectively by adopting broad attention strategies for low-involvement products and deep attention strategies for high-involvement products in the digital marketing environment. This paper contributes to a better understanding of attention allocation in marketing and provides both theoretical and practical implications for firms seeking to improve marketing effectiveness in the attention economy.

latest.title: Children’s responses to influencer advertising: examining the impact of advertising disclosure and content type
latest.abstract: Kidfluencers have become an increasingly familiar feature of children’s online viewing, raising concerns about how children process persuasive content embedded in entertainment. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model and advertising literacy, this study examines the effects of advertising disclosure and content type on children’s purchase intention, as well as the moderating role of advertising literacy. A quasi-experimental study using a 2 (disclosure vs. non-disclosure) × 3 (content type: rational, interactional, transactional) design was conducted with children aged 8–12 years using manipulated kidfluencer videos. Data were analyzed using two-way analysis of variance and moderation analysis. The results indicate that advertising disclosure had a significant effect on purchase intention. Children exposed to disclosed content reported higher purchase intention than those exposed to non-disclosed content. Content type and the interaction between disclosure and content type were not statistically significant. Advertising literacy also significantly moderated the effect of advertising disclosure on purchase intention, such that the positive effect of disclosure weakened as advertising literacy increased. These findings point to the importance of considering both disclosure practices and children’s advertising literacy when investigating responses to influencer advertising and suggest that advertising disclosure does not necessarily reduce children’s purchase intention.

latest.title: Exploring How to Optimize Enterprise Marketing Strategies in the Digital Age
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and the proliferation of new media platforms are fundamentally transforming the retail landscape and reshaping consumer decision-making processes. In this evolving environment, conventional, mass-oriented marketing approaches are increasingly inadequate for sustaining competitive advantage in digital markets—evidenced by persistently low customer acquisition efficiency and diminishing brand resonance. This paper systematically examines enterprise-level digital marketing strategies through a dual-method approach: comprehensive literature review and in-depth case analysis. It first maps the current state of the digital marketing ecosystem, then identifies and analyzes critical implementation barriers—including organizational silos, data fragmentation, and capability gaps—that hinder effective digital marketing adoption, further clarifies the core strategic advantages of digital marketing (e.g., real-time responsiveness, audience precision, and iterative optimization) and its tangible business value, and finally proposes forward-looking, actionable recommendations aligned with emerging industry trajectories. Empirical findings indicate that sustainable marketing transformation hinges on three interdependent pillars: seamless cross-channel integration, granular data-driven operationalization, and audience-centric content innovation. These insights provide a rigorous, practice-oriented framework to guide traditional enterprises in navigating their digital marketing transformation.

latest.title: Achieving sustainable development goals through digital supply chains: The interplay between green innovation, AI adoption, and consumer preferences
latest.abstract: The research investigates the impacts of AI adoption, green innovation, consumer preferences, and infrastructure on SDG-aligned supply chain performance in the Malaysian pharmaceutical industry. Additionally, the research examines the mediating role of trust in these relationships. Resource-Based View theory and the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework are the theoretical basis of this research. A quantitative research design was utilized to collect data from 325 pharmaceutical employees in Penang, Malaysia, by conducting a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed with SPSS for Descriptive Statistics and SmartPLS for Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that all direct relationships are significant, with green innovation, AI adoption, infrastructure, and consumer preferences having positive impacts on SDG-aligned supply chain performance. Additionally, trust proves to mediate these relationships and emerges as the strongest predictor of sustainable supply chain performance. The findings add to the literature by integrating the Resource-Based View and TOE, placing green innovation and AI as strategic assets of competitive advantage. Regarding the practical insights, it is recommended that companies invest in AI-powered sustainability analytics, jointly design green products with customers, create SDG 9-based key performance indicators, and focus on building trust based on open stakeholder relations, thus creating green supply chain management initiatives. Nevertheless, the study is limited by aspects such as its cross-sectional design and a focus on the region, so future longitudinal and multi-industry studies can increase the extent of generalizability and prove causality.

latest.title: AI features and social influence affect Gen Z purchase intention and behavior through trust in an extended SOR model
latest.abstract: Driven by digital transformation in the global retail sector, this study investigates the psychological and behavioral mechanisms underlying Generation Z college students’ AI-assisted shopping experiences. It examines how four stimuli—AI algorithm transparency, user-friendliness, internet word of mouth (IWOM), and trust propensity—influence consumer trust and purchase intention, alongside the moderating effects of privacy concern and information collection behavior. Drawing on an extended Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, the research empirically validates the proposed framework using 979 valid online survey responses analyzed via SPSS 32. Results reveal that the four antecedents exert significantly positive effects on both consumer trust and purchase intention, with trust serving as a significant mediator between these antecedents and purchase intention. Additionally, information collection behavior positively moderates the relationship between IWOM and consumer trust, while privacy concern negatively moderates the relationship between AI algorithm transparency and consumer trust. This study offers novel theoretical insights into Gen Z’s AI shopping behaviors and provides practical implications: retailers should enhance AI algorithm transparency, optimize user interfaces, cultivate positive IWOM, and strengthen privacy protection to foster Gen Z’s trust and facilitate purchase conversion.

latest.title: Cognitive bias across generations: The influence of online reviews on consumer decision-making in E-commerce
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: This study examines whether purchase intentions in response to online review scenarios differ across generational cohorts. Survey data were collected from 1028 Czech online panellists grouped into Baby Boomers, Generation X, Generation Y (Millennials), and Generation Z. Participants evaluated ten fictitious reviews developed around anchoring, attribute emphasis, framing, recency, and hindsight-related cues. Kruskal–Wallis tests yielded nominally significant cohort differences for positive anchoring, design-focused attribute emphasis, positive framing, and the older-review scenario. All four omnibus effect sizes were very small (η 2 H = 0.005–0.009). Holm-adjusted Dunn comparisons identified differences between Baby Boomers and Generations Y and Z for positive anchoring, between Baby Boomers and Generation Z for design-focused attribute emphasis, and between Baby Boomers and Generation Y for the older-review scenario. No pairwise comparison for positive framing remained significant after adjustment. These findings suggest that cohort membership alone provides limited information about responses to the scenarios and does not justify generation-specific review-interface strategies. The attribute-emphasis scenarios vary substantive product information and therefore do not isolate a priming mechanism. More generally, the Czech quota sample, hypothetical purchase-intention measures, and confounded stimuli restrict generalisability and causal interpretation. The study provides exploratory descriptive evidence rather than a basis for inferring stable generational differences in susceptibility to cognitive bias.

latest.title: Marketing innovation capability, market knowledge capability, and digital marketing capability on marketing performance: The mediating role of religiocentric relational advantage
latest.abstract: This study investigates the influence of marketing innovation capability (MIC), digital marketing capability (DMC), and market knowledge capability (MKC) on marketing performance (MP), with religiocentric relational advantage (RRA) as a mediating variable. Data were collected through questionnaires with 305 leaders or owners of Muslim fashion SMEs in Indonesia. The data were processed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). These findings show that marketing innovation capability, digital marketing capability, and market knowledge capability directly influence both religiocentric relational advantage and marketing performance. Furthermore, religiocentric relational advantage also directly influences marketing performance. Religiocentric relational advantage mediates the relationship between marketing innovation capability and marketing performance. Religiocentric relational advantage also mediates the relationship between digital marketing capability and marketing performance, and between market knowledge capability and marketing performance.

latest.title: The evolution and future directions of AI in digital marketing within the banking sector
latest.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) is changing digital marketing in the banking sector. The need to engage with consumers in a personalized, dynamic, and automated way has become a pressing requirement now that institutions that were formerly traditional, product-oriented are shifting to dynamic, customer-centric approaches. Although the field is growing rapidly in terms of technology, extensive syntheses of the new field are still in their early stages. Therefore, this study seeks to develop a systematic synthesis on the development, modern trends, and themes of AI use in digital marketing in the banking sector. Using a PRISMA-compliant systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis, a strict search was conducted in the Scopus and Web of Science databases, which returned 107 articles. After meeting the inclusion criteria, a final sample of 47 peer-reviewed journal articles, conference papers, book chapters, and review articles was selected for detailed assessment. The discussion reveals a big shift towards data-based, advanced marketing strategies. Besides, the bibliometric synthesis identifies major thematic groups that are currently prevalent in the academic world. These clusters include customer engagement, machine-learning-based customer segmentation and predictive analytics, automation and service personalization via chatbots, and advanced applications leveraging deep learning and recommendation systems. By leveraging these technologies together, banking institutions can provide more personalized communications, anticipate consumer behavior, and operate more efficiently. But, since this is a relatively new and emerging area of research, there are still critical gaps. The results point to the pressing needs of increased explainability of models t

latest.title: Secondary Market Premiums and Impulse Buying in Concert Ticketing: The Role of Scarcity, FOMO and Institutional Regulation
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: The secondary market premium of concert tickets represents a structurally embedded flaw in live entertainment markets, and it can strongly influence consumers' impulse purchasing. With Jay Chou's "Carnival" tour as a real-world example, this article combines the perspective of scarcity theory and fear of loss (FOMO) to analyze the impact of secondary market premium on consumers' impulsive purchases. Some findings indicate that secondary market premiums enhance ticket allocation efficiency, reinforce fan-community cohesion, and incentivize organizers to expand supply. However, these premiums also generate systemic risks, including irrational overpayment, algorithmic scalping monopolies, and regulatory lag, which collectively undermine market fairness and consumer welfare. To tackle these real-world difficulties, this article uses strategies such as technical counter-control and improvement of the real-name system, price limit, and transparency in the secondary market, enhancement of the regulatory framework, and industry self-discipline. The study also reveals the double-edged effect of secondary market premiums, which helps the performance ticket market to grow sustainably and consistently.

latest.title: Decision pathways in mobile-app shopping: a Throughput Model study of online consumers
latest.abstract: Purpose Mobile shopping environments increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to personalise recommendations, curate product information and support purchase decisions. Yet, existing consumer decision-making models maintain a linear, stage-based logic that fails to capture how AI-enabled interfaces compress, extend or reconfigure the pathways consumers actually follow. This study aims to use the Throughput Model (TPM) to conceptualise and empirically validate distinct algorithmic decision pathways through which perception, information search and evaluative judgement interact to shape purchase intentions in mobile-app shopping contexts. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from Gen Z consumers with recent mobile-app shopping experience. The study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and mediation analysis to test the TPM and estimate one-step, two-step and three-step decision pathways in AI-enabled mobile commerce. Findings Perception, information search and judgement each exert significant effects within the model, with judgement emerging as the central integrative mechanism linking upstream inputs to purchase intention. These results demonstrate that AI-enabled mobile interfaces simultaneously support impulsive, efficiency-driven and deliberative decision architectures. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first empirical operationalisation of the TPM in mobile-app commerce, reconceptualising purchase decisions as coexisting algorithmic pathways rather than a single sequential route. It offers marketers a diagnostic framework for segmenting consumers by decision architecture and designing adaptive AI-enabled shopping experiences accordingly.

latest.title: Drivers of sustainable fashion purchase in India: a moderated value framework
latest.abstract: Purpose Although sustainable fashion research has extensively examined either consumer attitudes or purchase intentions, limited studies have explicitly distinguished between the cognitive foundation of attitude and the situationally driven nature of intention within the eco-fashion context. Furthermore, the interactive role of psychological traits such as altruism and mindfulness, along with economic considerations like willingness to pay a premium, in moderating the attitude–intention relationship remains underexplored, particularly in emerging markets such as India. This study aims to address these gaps by developing and empirically validating an integrated framework that captures both individual and contextual drivers of eco-fashion purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comprehensive mixed-methods design informed by grounded theory principles, this study explores the underlying factors that shape the phenomenon. Qualitative data from interviews and FGD enabled themes to emerge inductively, while quantitative survey data validated and extended these insights. Statistical analyses examined relationships among variables, and hypotheses were tested using SEM to ensure robustness of the conceptual model. Findings Environmental consciousness, social influence and marketing stimuli considerably shape eco-fashion attitude and purchase intention, while attitude mediates these relationships. Altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay strengthen the relationship between attitude and purchase intention. Originality/value The study proposes a moderated value framework that explains sustainable fashion purchase more dynamically by treating altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay as moderators in the Indian context.

latest.title: Tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng của người tiêu dùng trẻ trong mua sắm livestream: bằng chứng từ ngành thời trang Việt Nam
latest.venue: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: Trong lĩnh vực livestream thời trang tại Việt Nam, hành vi ra quyết định mua của nhóm khách hàng trẻ chịu ảnh hưởng bởi các tín hiệu xã hội, đặc biệt là cảm giác sợ bỏ lỡ và xu hướng hành động theo đám đông. Dựa trên khung Kích thích – Chủ thể – Phản hồi (S-O-R), nghiên cứu kiểm định tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ (FoMO) và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng, đồng thời phân tích vai trò trung gian của trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng. Dữ liệu 308 người tiêu dùng trẻ đã tham gia mua sắm livestream thời trang được phân tích bằng PLS-SEM. Kết quả cho thấy, FoMO và hiệu ứng đám đông đều ảnh hưởng tích cực đến trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng và hành vi mua bốc đồng. Trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng đóng vai trò trung gian một phần. Nghiên cứu góp phần cung cấp thêm bằng chứng thực nghiệm trong livestream commerce ngành thời trang tại Việt Nam và gợi ý hàm ý quản trị cho doanh nghiệp.

latest.title: Modeling Circularwashing Risk in Renewable Energy Adoption: A Structural Equation Approach for Sustainable Consumption
latest.abstract: Abstract Circularwashing limits eco-friendly consumption by overstating, confusing, or inadequately proving the circular properties of products. While regular greenwashing makes ambiguous claims about the environmental characteristics, circularwashing takes advantage of the complicated nature of resource loops and the quality of the supply chain, causing significant market friction and high information asymmetry. Hence, an unexpected change in information distorts price signals, weakens customer trust, and jeopardizes market transparency by creating a lemon market for real circular goods. The present research presents the idea of circularwashing risk and provides a model to analyze the effect of false claims on the customers’ skepticism, decision-making risk perception, institutional trust, penalties for unreasonable behavior, and post-decision actions. The model is based on the Signaling Theory and the Stimulus Organism Response theory and is verified with the help of the survey data collected from 607 digital consumers in Colombia using the method of Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Model (PLS SEM). The measurement properties were assessed through composite reliability, average variance extracted, and heterotrait monotrait discriminant criteria and bootstrap resampling. The findings imply that misleading environmental claims correlate with consumer skepticism, which has a positive relationship with perceived decision risks and the erosion of institutional trust. Moreover, the effects of perceived decision risk and erosion of institutional trust on behavioral penalty are considerable. Structural chains indicate that the relationship between decision risk and erosion of trust serves as two mediating channels. Lastly, the Circularwashing Risk Propagation Model s

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Personalizing Social Media Marketing Strategies for Enhanced Customer Experience
hot.abstract: This paper explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in personalizing social media marketing strategies and its impact on customer experience, with a focus on consumers within the MENA region. Using data collected from an online questionnaire completed by 893 individuals, the study confirms that AI significantly enhances social media marketing by offering personalized content, optimizing influencer selection, and enabling real-time consumer interaction. These capabilities not only increase customer awareness but also improve user experience and purchase intentions. Key AI tools such as influencer marketing, content optimization, and customization are effective in capturing consumer attention, although further research is necessary to deepen understanding. By examining AI's ability to analyze vast datasets and support targeted marketing efforts, the study contributes to both academic and practical discourse, offering insights that businesses can use to refine their AI-driven social media strategies. Ultimately, the research aims to guide marketers through the complexities of AI deployment, ensuring its benefits are fully realized for consumers.

hot.title: The Role of Environmental Certification in the Hospitality Industry: Assessing Sustainability, Consumer Preferences, and the Economic Impact
hot.abstract: Hotel certifications have become increasingly vital in promoting sustainability within the hospitality industry, providing frameworks that guide hotels toward reducing their environmental footprint, enhancing operational efficiency, and gaining a competitive edge in the marketplace. This review explores the development, types, and impact of hotel certifications, with a focus on prominent schemes, such as LEED, Green Key, and EarthCheck. Through an analysis of case studies from globally recognized hotels, we highlight how certifications contribute to significant reductions in energy and water use, improved waste management, and enhanced biodiversity protection, while also delivering economic benefits through cost savings and increased guest loyalty. Our paper also examines consumer perceptions of certifications and their willingness to pay (WTP) for certified hotels. The findings suggest that eco-conscious travelers, particularly younger generations, are willing to pay a premium for hotels that demonstrate a commitment to sustainability; however, consumer awareness of certification schemes remains limited. The barriers to adopting certifications, such as high initial costs, resource limitations, and management resistance, are also discussed, along with the challenges posed by greenwashing and the proliferation of certification schemes. Looking to the future, this review identifies key trends that will shape the evolution of hotel certifications, including increased transparency, the integration of smart technologies, the expanding role of social responsibility, and their alignment with global sustainability goals, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
