latest.title: Strategic Agility and Sustainable Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Nakuru County, Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: Strategic agility is the capacity of a firm to sense changes in its operating environment, anticipate alternative futures and reconfigure its resources and operations in good time. It has become a critical capability for manufacturing firms, which operate in an increasingly uncertain environment characterised by economic instability, supply chain disruptions, climate variability and rising production costs. In Nakuru County, Kenya, many manufacturing firms still respond to such disruptions reactively, and evidence on how agility practices relate to their ability to sustain performance remains limited. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the influence of strategic agility on sustainable performance of manufacturing firms in Nakuru County, Kenya. It explored four practices, namely environmental scanning, scenario planning, strategic flexibility and early warning systems. The study was anchored on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Complexity Theory, the Resource-Based View and Organizational Learning Theory. The study adopted a descriptive and explanatory research design and targeted the 34 manufacturing firms in the county. A census of the firms was undertaken and four managers, comprising senior, operations and strategy managers, were purposively selected from each firm, giving 136 respondents, of whom 96 returned completed questionnaires. Structured questionnaires were used to collect data. Both descriptive and inferential statistical methods were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four practices jointly explained 43.9% of the variation in sustainable performance. Environmental scanning was the strongest predictor of sustainable performance, followed by scenario planning and early warning sys

latest.title: Beyond Rational Choice: A Behavioral Game-Theoretic Frameworkfor Consumer Decision-Making
latest.venue: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
latest.abstract: Since Behavioral Economics explains decisions through bounded rationality and mental shortcuts, it is necessary to incorporate strategic interactions into such analyses. This study develops an integrated framework for analyzing irrational purchasing decisions, which includes elements of Behavioral Economics, non-cooperative Game Theory, econometric analysis, and an integrated model of consumer behavior, the Consumer Irrational Utility Model (CIUM). The study employs a quantitative survey of personal care products consumers in the FMCG market, modeling a consumer and a seller as two players in a 2 × 2 non-cooperative game. The game is analyzed using best-response strategies, followed by the derivation of a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium. The results of the game-theoretic model are then tested using Linear Probability Model (LPM) and Weighted Least Squares (WLS) for estimation purposes. The results of the behavioral determinants, validated in the LPM and WLS estimations, are then incorporated into CIUM, which explains how irrational behavior by a consumer deviates from the utility-maximizing behavior of a rational human being. The study reveals that in the Indian FMCG market, consumers mainly adopt the Relative Decision Paradox strategy, whereas sellers mainly adopt the Strategized Pricing strategy. The study further reveals that the behavioral variables identified in the study have a significant impact on consumers' purchasing decisions. Also, results from the CIUM indicate that the economic utility of a product and the utility influenced by various behavioral factors in strategic interactions in the market jointly determine the overall utility of a product for a consumer.

latest.title: Integrating Social Influence Theory and the Theory of Planned Behavior to Explain Green Drinkware Purchase Intention among Jakarta’s Emerging Adults: The Moderating Role of Economic Constraints
latest.abstract: This study investigated how digital social influence shaped green drinkware purchase intentions among emerging adults in Jakarta by integrating Social Influence Theory (SIT) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). A quantitative survey was conducted among 400 Jakarta residents aged 20–29 who were familiar with green drinkware and had previously used or purchased such products. The collected data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings revealed that social media engagement positively influenced attitudes and subjective norms, with the relationship between social media engagement and subjective norms exhibiting the strongest path coefficient. Both attitudes and subjective norms positively influenced green label awareness, which, in turn, strengthened green brand trust. Green brand trust subsequently had a positive effect on green purchase intention. Although economic constraints exhibited a negative moderating effect, this relationship was not statistically significant. These findings indicated that social media served not merely as an information dissemination channel but also as a normative environment that shaped consumers' perceptions, attitudes, and behavioral intentions. Furthermore, green purchase intention emerged through a multistage process involving social influence, psychological responses, environmental information awareness, and brand trust. The study contributed to the integration of SIT and TPB by demonstrating the interconnected mechanisms underlying environmentally responsible purchasing intentions. From a practical perspective, the findings highlighted the importance of leveraging social proof in marketing communications, providing credible environmental labeling information, strengthening consume

latest.title: AI digital humans and destination marketing: the multidimensionality of anthropomorphism, parasocial interactions and marketing effectiveness
latest.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Insights
latest.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) digital humans, developed to mimic humans, have emerged as promoters in marketing. Although existing studies have identified that AI digital humans' anthropomorphism shapes marketing outcomes, the multidimensionality of anthropomorphism remains underexplored. Focusing on historical figure-inspired AI digital humans in tourism destination marketing, this study examines how their multiple anthropomorphic features influence consumers' responses under the Computers are Social Actors and Media are Social Actors paradigms. Design/methodology/approach An online survey (N = 435) was conducted in 2026. Respondents completed a questionnaire after watching a typical travel vlog featuring a historical figure-based AI digital human. Findings We revealed that voice, behavior and mental anthropomorphism influence consumers' parasocial interactions with AI digital humans, which subsequently affect consumers' attitudes toward tourism destinations. Mental anthropomorphism mediates appearance, voice and behavior anthropomorphism's effects on parasocial interactions. Furthermore, mental anthropomorphism's effect is conditioned by consumers' familiarity with the AI digital human's historical figure prototype. Research limitations/implications This study extends existing research by demonstrating that AI digital humans' multiple anthropomorphic features shape consumers' parasocial interactions, with historical figure familiarity serving as a moderator. However, nonprobability sampling and a single cultural context restrict generalizability, warranting cross-cultural research with probability sampling in the future. Practical implications This study provides practical insight into developing AI digital humans in tourism marketing. Marketers should systemat

latest.title: Anthropomorphism and emotional reactions to human–AI collaboration.
latest.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly enters human professional domains, understanding emotional reactions to its involvement becomes critical.We introduce a novel experimental paradigm that distinguishes between AI involvement in "Thinker" and "Doer" roles to examine how the role AI occupies shapes affective and evaluative responses to human-AI collaboration.Across four countries (N = 1,345), including the United States, the United Kingdom, India, and Colombia, participants evaluated scenarios in which professional jobs were completed under four conditions: human only, full AI automation, human as Thinker with AI as Doer, or AI as Thinker with human as Doer.Our results showed that AI involvement decreased positive affect and appreciation while increasing negative affect.We also found particularly negative emotional reactions to AI executing emotionally charged professions (e.g., artist).Individual differences in AI anthropomorphism consistently moderated these effects.These findings demonstrate that emotional reactions to AI depend on the role it plays and the domain in which it operates.This research highlights the importance of task characteristics and individual differences in understanding human-AI collaboration in professional settings.

latest.title: Public–Private Partnerships in Defence Manufacturing: Performance,Risk Sharing and Accountability
latest.venue: International Journal of Engineering Technology and Management Sciences
latest.abstract: World military expenditure reached US$2,718 billion in 2024, a real rise of 9.4% and the steepest annual increase since at least 1988, and governments now ask private manufacturers to expand defence output faster than state arsenals can. Public–private partnerships (PPPs) are the main contractual vehicle for this, yet the evidence on whether they deliver value, how they share risk, and who answers for failure is scattered across audit reports, policy documents and a thin academic literature. This review synthesises 101 sources published up to October 2026 on PPPs in defence manufacturing and support, drawn from the United Kingdom, the United States and India. It then develops a Performance–Risk–Accountability (PRA) framework that links a risk-adjusted value-for-money test, an optimal cost-sharing rule and an accountability condition for contestability. Four findings stand out. The UK National Audit Office could not conclude that the £10.5 billion, 27-year tanker PFI achieved value for money, and negotiations took over nine years. The UK government-owned, contractor-operated reform of defence procurement collapsed in 2013 with one bidder. India's private sector raised its share of defence production from 21% to 23% in FY2024-25, while only 14.5% of Rs 74,756 crore of corridor investment commitments had been grounded by April 2026. The framework implies that high-uncertainty development work should carry low private cost shares, mature serial production high shares, and that accountability fails when the state cannot credibly replace its partner.

latest.title: Digital and social media marketing: a bibliometric mapping from 2020 to 2025
latest.abstract: Abstract Digital and social media marketing is reshaping how firms communicate with consumers, gather market intelligence, manage customer journeys, and build brand relationships. This study followed the PRISMA framework to select relevant Scopus-indexed articles between 2020 and 2025 under the business, management, and accounting subject area, using the search terms “digital marketing” and “social media marketing” in titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search, conducted on 20 February 2026 and restricted to open-access, English-language, final-stage journal articles, yielded 1,054 articles. Performance analysis, citation analysis, author-keyword co-occurrence mapping, an average-publication-year overlay, co-citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling were conducted using VOSviewer. Findings reveal publication growth, particularly during 2024 and 2025. Indonesia was the leading country by publications, whereas the UK was the most influential country by citations. Additionally, the “Journal of Business Research” is the most influential, while “Cogent Business & Management” is the most productive journal; the most-cited document is “Setting the future of digital and social media marketing research: Perspectives and research propositions,” with 1,806 citations, produced by “International Journal of Information Management.” Four of the ten prominent authors published six papers each, including Saura, J.R., and Huertas-Garcia, R., both affiliated with Spanish institutions. Keyword mapping identifies digital marketing, social media marketing, social media, consumer behavior, marketing, and purchase intention as central themes. This study clarifies the post-2020 knowledge structure of the open-access segment of this literature, proposes that digital and social media marketi

latest.title: Analisys detection place defect incoming part in the incoming quality control division at PT XYZ cikarang
latest.venue: TEKNOSAINS Jurnal Sains Teknologi dan Informatika
latest.abstract: The quality of incoming parts is a critical factor affecting the quality of final products in the electronics manufacturing industry. Nonconforming materials received from suppliers can increase product defects, production costs, and disrupt manufacturing processes. This study aims to analyze incoming part defects in the Incoming Quality Control (IQC) Division of PT XYZ Cikarang based on defect types, defect detection locations, root causes, and improvement priorities. The study employed Seven Tools, Fishbone Diagram, and Failure Mode and Effect Analysis (FMEA) using data from the Incoming Production Rework Report for February 2026. The data were analyzed using check sheets, Pareto diagrams, defect detection place analysis, Fishbone diagrams, and FMEA. The results revealed that scratch was the dominant defect, accounting for 58.66% of the 358 recorded defects, while the highest-risk failure cause was the non-optimal material handling standard operating procedure, with a Risk Priority Number (RPN) of 504. Based on these findings, improvement priorities were focused on revising material handling procedures, enhancing operator competency, standardizing supplier packing methods, and improving material storage systems. This study contributes by integrating Seven Tools, Fishbone Diagram, and FMEA to establish a systematic risk-based approach for prioritizing quality improvement actions, thereby supporting more effective incoming material quality control in electronics manufacturing

latest.title: Hybrid Markov Regime-Switching and Hurdle modeling of last-mile livestock logistics in Ukraine under systemic volatility
latest.abstract: Abstract This study examines the transformation of last-mile logistics in Ukraine’s livestock supply chains under conditions of prolonged systemic volatility and infrastructure disruption. A hybrid analytical framework is proposed that integrates Random Forest Recursive Feature Elimination (RF-RFE) for preliminary predictor screening, a two-state Markov Regime-Switching (MRS) model for identifying latent logistics regimes, and a two-part Hurdle model for separately estimating disruption probability and conditional freight-cost intensity. The empirical analysis uses a verified monthly panel dataset covering 2023–2025 across three contrasting regional logistics nodes - Kyiv, Vinnytsia, and Lviv - and incorporates energy, security, market, transport, and infrastructure-related indicators. The MRS results identify two statistically distinct and persistent freight-cost regimes, with the systemic-crisis regime characterized by a 21.8% higher mean Freight Cost Per Ton and a longer expected duration than the operational-stability regime. The Hurdle estimates show that Security Alerts and Power Outage Hours are positively associated with the probability of logistics disruption, while Power Outage Hours and Fuel Price Volatility are positively associated with conditional freight-cost intensity; regional comparisons further reveal heterogeneous exposure to systemic shocks. Counterfactual technological scenarios further indicate that combining AI-assisted dynamic routing with decentralized autonomous and light electric transport solutions could reduce the estimated sensitivity of freight costs to energy disruptions by approximately 24.2%. The findings demonstrate the value of combining latent-regime identification, sequential disruption modeling, and technological scenario analysis

latest.title: Corporate Crisis and Disaster Management in the Digital Era: Building Organisational Resilience through Digital Transformation
latest.venue: British Journal of Computer Networking and Information Technology
latest.abstract: Corporate crises are increasingly shaped by interconnected digital infrastructures, global supply chains, cloud services, artificial intelligence and data-intensive business models. This conceptual article examines how digital transformation is changing the character and management of corporate crises. It develops an integrated Digital Crisis Resilience Framework (DCRF). Drawing on crisis management, organisational resilience, dynamic capabilities, stakeholder and socio-technical systems theories, the article conceptualises resilience as a continuous strategic capability rather than a reactive emergency function. The DCRF integrates eight capabilities across the crisis lifecycle. Comparative analysis of the NotPetya/Maersk, SolarWinds, COVID-19, Colonial Pipeline and CrowdStrike cases illuminates the Digital Resilience Paradox: digitalisation can simultaneously strengthen adaptive capacity and increase systemic vulnerability. A five-level Digital Crisis Resilience Maturity Model, research propositions and an implementation roadmap are proposed. The article contributes by integrating fragmented research streams and extending crisis resilience from the firm level to the wider digital ecosystem.

latest.title: Adaptive Decision-Making in Action: Decision-Maker Profiles Under Time Pressure and Incomplete Information
latest.venue: Journal of Intelligence Studies in Business
latest.abstract: Competitive intelligence increasingly requires decision-makers to extract actionable signals from abundant, incomplete, and rapidly changing information within compressed timeframes. Although decision research has extensively examined analytical and intuitive reasoning, less is known about how these modes combine into distinct person-level configurations. Using survey data from 246 employees and a person-centred analytical approach, K-means clustering based on Analytical Orientation, Intuitive Orientation, and Contextual Adaptability identified four distinct profiles: an Analysis-Dominant Profile, an Intuition-Dominant Profile, a Context-Adaptive Profile, and an Analytical–Intuitive Integrative Profile. External validation revealed a significant Profile × Analytical Burden interaction, LR χ²(3) = 29.00, p < .001, indicating that the association between Analytical Burden and negative responses to time pressure differed across profiles. The study develops the concept of Adaptive Decision-Making in Action, defined as the capability to maintain, switch, substitute, or integrate analytical and intuitive reasoning according to situational demands. The findings extend CI research beyond the analytical-intuitive dichotomy by showing that decision-making may take distinct configurational forms and suggest that decision development should focus on the adaptive use of decision modes rather than on a single preferred style.

latest.title: Will AI Replace Human Customer Relationship Managers? Advantages and Ethical Implications
latest.abstract: The growing use of autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents in customer-facing operations raises a practical question for customer relationship management (CRM): can systems designed to automate interactions take over the work traditionally performed by human relationship managers? This conceptual paper examines that question by bringing together research on AI-enabled marketing, automated service agents, customer trust and ethical human–technology interaction. The analysis distinguishes the completion of individual service tasks from the broader responsibility of sustaining customer relationships. The literature indicates that AI can handle many predictable, information-intensive activities, including responding to standard enquiries, retrieving account information and supporting routine transactions. Yet efficiency in these settings should not be interpreted as evidence that automated agents can consistently manage ambiguity, emotional strain, exceptions or consequential decisions. The paper develops a framework based on three assessment dimensions: operational suitability, relational suitability and ethical acceptability. These dimensions inform three possible service arrangements: AI substitution for bounded tasks, AI augmentation of employee work, and human-led handling of complex or sensitive encounters. Six propositions are advanced for empirical investigation. The paper argues that the future of CRM is more likely to involve a redistribution of responsibilities than the wholesale elimination of human relationship managers. Its contribution is to connect task performance with relationship quality and responsible governance when organizations decide how much authority to delegate to AI.

latest.title: Intelligent Automation and Sustainable Performance of Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria: A Critical Review of the Roles of Operational Efficiency, Employee Adaptability and Organizational Agility
latest.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
latest.abstract: Intelligent automation is revolutionizing banking from digitization of consumer transactions to integration of robotic process automation, artificial intelligence, analytics, and connected workflows. Deposit money banks in Nigeria are making efforts in this regard to cut down costs, improve service quality, manage fraud, and cope up with competition from digitally minded financial service companies. But acquisition of technologies does not mean sustainable performance. This paper aims to critically assess how intelligent automation may affect the sustainable performance of deposit money banks in Nigeria in terms of finance, operations, people, and institutions. In this regard, this paper takes the form of a narrative and conceptual review where the focus is primarily on Nigerian literature but using international literature to draw theory and context comparison. The review finds out that there are three major interrelated explanatory mechanisms such as operational efficiency, adaptive capacity of employees, and organizational agility. With automation, banks can achieve faster, accurate, scalable, compliant, and supported decisions. On the other hand, these benefits can be hampered by incompatibility with legacy systems, lack of data, security risks, high cost of implementation, resistance from employees, skill mismatches, and poor governance. Using socio-technical systems theory, task-technology fit theory, resource-based view, dynamic capability theory, and human capital theory, this article presents a conceptual understanding of intelligent automation in the context of socio-technical organizational capabilities rather than being just a technology. This study pinpoints some conceptual ambiguity, short-sightedness about performance, weak indicators of automation maturi

latest.title: An Explainable AI Framework for Marketing Customer Segmentation and Campaign Response Prediction
latest.venue: The American Journal of Engineering And Technology
latest.abstract: The segmentation of clients and the forecast of marketing campaign response are essential for optimising marketing expenditures and enhancing customer participation. This work suggests an XAI approach for segmenting the clients, predicting the responses using machine learning, and targeting them based on profit. Specifically, 2,055 cleansed customer records were extracted from the Kaggle Customer Personality Analysis dataset through preprocessing. We combine multiple clustering methods using consensus clustering to find the different segments of consumers, using Principal Component Analysis (PCA). The performance of seven machine learning classifiers is assessed using five-fold cross-validation, considering several performance metrics. The best accuracy (ACC) is 87.59% for Gradient Boosting (GB) and the ROC-AUC is 0.909 for Logistic Regression. The segment integration yields an improved recall (REC) rate of 79.4% and F1 score (F1) of 0.649, compared to the previous situation of REC value 73.0% and F1 value 0.622. The resulting profit-optimised solution is a projected profit of 61.1 currency units per 100 consumers. Moreover, elements such as catalogue purchases, recency, and campaign history are identified as elements that are significant via the techniques of SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and permutation feature significance. The proposed approach will enable more accurate client segmentation, targeted marketing campaigns, and efficient use of resources. More testing is needed on a variety of real-life datasets to ensure greater generalisability, but the outcomes are encouraging.

latest.title: Sustainable Supply Chain Management in Semiconductor Manufacturing: Strategies, Challenges, and Integrative Models for Future Prospects
latest.venue: American International Journal of Supply Chain Management
latest.abstract: The semiconductor industry underpins modern technology, yet chip fabrication is energy-, water- and chemical-intensive, consumes close to 1% of global electricity, and depends on critical minerals sourced through geographically dispersed supply chains. This study examines how sustainable supply chain management (SSCM) can address the environmental, social and economic challenges of semiconductor manufacturing by integrating the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework with the Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) model. The study employs a qualitative, literature-based design that combines a review of 26 scholarly sources with secondary data from corporate sustainability disclosures and industry estimates for 2022–2030 and illustrative cases of Intel, TSMC and Samsung, organised around four dependent, six independent and three control variables. The results show that sector energy consumption is projected to rise from about 227 TWh in 2022 to 319 TWh in 2030, while hazardous waste generation increases from 1.5 to 1.9 million tons over the same period. Reported recycling rates of leading firms range from 68% to 100%, SSCM adopters record cost savings of 10–15%, and the market valuation premium associated with sustainable practice rises from 20% in 2023 to a projected 30% by 2030. The findings of this study suggest that environmental performance is highly sensitive to site and watershed conditions, that company-level efficiency gains coexist with rising absolute energy use, that resilience and sustainability are related but not synonymous and may conflict in the short term through higher supply chain costs, and that evidence on circularity and digital technologies in semiconductor supply chains remains limited. latest.title: Analysis of fractional-order evolutionary behaviors between governments and logistics enterprises with interval parameters
latest.abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and sustainable development, green logistics represents the core direction of logistics industry transformation. To handle the uncertainty of benefits and losses in the green transition, this paper introduces interval two-dimensional linear differential equations, and constructs integer-order (IO) and fractional-order (FO) evolutionary game models with interval parameters. It explores the government’s regulatory paths for the green transition of logistics enterprises under uncertain benefits and reward-punishment mechanisms. Based on stability theory, we analyze the government-enterprise evolutionary patterns and compare the two models under the static reward-penalty mechanism (SRPM). The results indicate that under SRPM, the two models exhibit consistent stability of boundary equilibrium points but differ in the stability of internal equilibrium points. For dynamic schemes, the interior equilibrium of the integer-order model is locally asymptotically stable (LAS) if subsidies are lower than fines. Under specific conditions, the upper and lower bounds of interval parameters affect the evolutionary stability of equilibrium points. This study provides theoretical support for the regulation of green transition in logistics.

latest.title: Digital marketing and information technologies in corporate reporting governance: A quantitative and regulatory assessment
latest.abstract: Digital corporate reporting extends beyond publishing financial statements to the systems used to prepare disclosures and the channels through which companies communicate with stakeholders. Yet these elements are seldom examined together, from a governance perspective. This study develops the Corporate Reporting Digital Maturity Index (CRDMI) and applies it to eight companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange in 2024. The index comprises information technology capability (ITC), digital marketing integration (DMI), and reporting accessibility and interactivity (RAI). A cross-sectional review of publicly available materials was undertaken. Observable indicators were assigned scores from zero to two, normalized, and combined using equal weights for the three dimensions. Sensitivity analysis examined whether alternative weighting assumptions changed the comparative results. Technology-oriented firms generally scored higher than companies in industrial and consumer sectors. Digital marketing integration showed the greatest variation, indicating uneven connections between reporting and broader online communication. The findings suggest that investment in reporting infrastructure does not necessarily translate into easier access to information or more meaningful stakeholder interaction. CRDMI offers a transparent starting point for assessment, rather than a direct measure of disclosure quality or compliance. Given the small, purposively selected sample, testing with larger samples, independent coders, and longitudinal evidence is warranted.

latest.title: From others to the self: Influence mechanisms of multiple social agents on sustainable consumption
latest.abstract: 摘要： 可持续消费研究长期聚焦个体消费者的心理与行为机制, 无力弥合可持续态度与实际消费行为之间的显著差距。理论演进的脉络梳理表明, 可持续消费的个体选择会受到消费者社会关系网络中多元社会主体的复杂影响。本文系统梳理个体、群体和组织层面的社会主体对消费者可持续消费的影响, 并基于自我决定理论提出了以基本心理需求和动机内化连续体为核心的社会主体影响机制与效应框架。未来研究应重点探讨如何完善多元主体对个体可持续消费的影响机制框架、拓展社会主体的研究边界、推动可持续消费的集体行动研究转向, 从而为破解可持续消费知易行难的现实困境拓展理论空间与实践路径。

latest.title: Pengaruh Influencer Marketing dan Online Customer Review terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Implora di TikTok Shop Cibinong
latest.abstract: Perkembangan pemasaran digital telah mengubah perilaku konsumen dalam melakukan pembelian melalui platform media sosial, salah satunya Tiktok Shop. Influencer Marketing dan Online Customer Review diduga menjadi faktor yang memengaruhi keputusan pembelian konsumen, khususnya pada produk kosmetik lokal Implora. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Influencer Marketing dan Online Customer Review terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Produk Implora di Tiktok Shop Kecamatan Cibinong, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan teknik purposive sampling berdasarkan formula Hair, sehingga diperoleh 120 responden. Analisis data dilakukan melalui uji validitas, uji reliabilitas, uji asumsi klasik, analisis regresi linier berganda, uji koefisien determinasi, uji t, dan uji F dengan bantuan SPSS. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Influencer Marketing berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Keputusan Pembelian (thitung 6,241 > ttabel 1,980; sig. 0,000 < 0,05). Online Customer Review juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Keputusan Pembelian (thitung 10,939 > ttabel 1,980; sig. 0,000 < 0,05). Secara simultan, kedua variabel berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Keputusan Pembelian (Fhitung 75,970 > Ftabel 3,07), dengan kontribusi sebesar 56,5%, sedangkan 43,5% sisanya dipengaruhi oleh faktor lain di luar penelitian ini. The development of digital marketing has changed consumer shopping behavior through social media, including TikTok Shop. Influencer Marketing and Online Customer Review are considered factors that influence consumer purchasing decisions. This study aims to analyze the partial and simultaneous effects of Influencer Marketing and Online Customer Review on purchasing decisions for Implora cosmetic

latest.title: AI-Powered E-Commerce Solutions for Smarter Retail Management and Customer Engagement
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Running an ecommerce business involves more than displaying products and processing orders. Retailers must understand customer preferences, maintain accurate product information, manage inventory, and provide timely assistance across multiple channels. As product catalogues and customer expectations grow, managing these activities manually becomes increasingly difficult. An AI E-Commerce Development Company can help businesses introduce intelligent tools that simplify retail operations, improve product discovery, and create more relevant customer experiences. Using AI to Understand Customer Behaviour Customer behaviour provides useful information about what shoppers need and how they interact with an online store. Product views, search queries, cart activity, and purchase history can reveal patterns that help businesses improve their services. AI-based analytics can process these signals to identify customer interests and purchasing trends. For example, an online retailer may use customer activity to understand which product categories receive the most attention or where shoppers frequently leave the purchasing journey. An AI-enabled ecommerce platform can support: Customer segmentation Purchase pattern analysis Personalised product suggestions Shopping behaviour insights Cart abandonment analysis Campaign performance evaluation These insights can help marketing and ecommerce teams make more informed decisions. However, recommendations should be based on relevant, appropriately collected data rather than assumptions about individual customers. Creating an AI E-Commerce Website With Intelligent Features An AI E-Commerce Website combines standard shopping functionality with intelligent features that support different stages of the customer journey. A typical platform may

latest.title: THE FUTURE OF BANKING: FINTECH REGULATION AND TRANSFORMATION OF FINANCIAL SERVICES IN NIGERIA
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The Study appraised the Future of Banking: Fintech, Regulation and Transformation of Financial System, analyzing the implication for traditional financial institutions. Methodologically, survey design was employed with data sourced from selected account holders of both Fintech and traditional banks in Ikot Ekpene Local Government area metropolis. Beside the use of questionnaire, personal observations were carried out as data collection technique in addition to the secondary data sourced from relevant textbooks, journals, newspaper and Internet. Moreover, the study assessed the rating of respondents on customer services provided by both Fintech and traditional banks. As well, the identifiable customer services gaps in traditional banks were assessed. Moreso, findings revealed that Fintech and traditional banks differ significantly on customer services with notable areas of customer satisfactory services provided by Fintech over traditional banks to include faster and more accessibility to credit, easy account opening and set-ups, convenience and stress free, instant transfers, friendliness, innovative solution to the needs of customers, digital inclusion penetration with youth population and cordial customer relationship (addressing complaint swiftly). On service gaps in traditional banks, the study identified inefficient modern banking techniques, unreliable digital infrastructure and relative financial inclusion. In light of the findings, the study recommended that the traditional banks should develop modern banking technique such as artificial Intelligence (AI) and machine learning in financial service, invest aggressively in technology. As well, CBN should continue to tighten oversight supervisory function to mitigate cybersecurity threat and streamline the multiple

latest.title: The use of generative artificial intelligence as a mental health resource: a rapid review on prevalence, conceptual boundaries, and public health implications
latest.abstract: Generative AI is already being used as a mental health resource by a considerable proportion of the population.Among the most robust estimates, 16% of US adults and 25% of adolescents in England and Wales reported using genAI for explicit mental health advice or support during the preceding 12 months.Recent nationally representative surveys suggest even more widespread use: 48% of people aged 16-39 in Germany reported discussing general psychological issues with genAI and 51% of those aged 18-34 in Czechia reported using these tools for mental health or emotional problems within preceding 30 days.These numbers also illustrate a key problem in the evidence base: studies measure different behaviors under the broad label of mental health-related use.To improve interpretation and future measurement, this review distinguishes three layers: i) companionship and social interaction, ii) emotional support and self-regulation, and iii) explicit mental health advice and support.Substantial methodological differences remain even within these layers, and reliable population estimates from low and middle income countries are largely absent.Better standardized and repeated monitoring is needed to understand the scale and development of this rapidly evolving public health phenomenon.

latest.title: Understanding data ecosystems: Conceptual foundations of the phenomenon
latest.abstract: Abstract Data ecosystems are increasingly recognized as critical to digital supply chains as they enable firms to access, exchange, govern, and mobilize data for coordinated action. These complex sociotechnical networks enable diverse stakeholders to engage in generating, sharing, and processing data, thereby fostering value creation across various industries. Yet despite growing interest, literature still lacks a consolidated understanding of what constitutes a data ecosystem and how its core elements interrelate. To address these issues, the present study employs a multimethod research design comprising a systematic literature review and a case study involving eight data ecosystem actors. The findings identify four constitutive subsystems of the data ecosystem: stakeholders, infrastructure, data, and governance, along with their underlying components. The study identifies six interrelations among these components, showing that data ecosystems depend not only on the presence of core elements but also on the relationships among them. By integrating insights from prior literature with empirical evidence, the study develops a foundation for understanding data ecosystems. The paper contributes to information systems (IS) research by clarifying the sociotechnical structure of data ecosystems and by providing a basis for future theorizing on interorganizational data sharing, governance, and responsive digital supply chains.

latest.title: Delving into AI disclosure architecture: Building trust in Indonesian telemedicine advertising
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractAI disclosure has become increasingly important in digital advertising, particularly in high-risk services such as telemedicine, where consumers evaluate message quality alongside provider accountability. This study aimed to examine how AI disclosure architecture, reflected in disclosure timing, disclosure specificity, and human control, influences perceived authenticity, message credibility, brand trust, and usage intention in Indonesian telemedicine advertising. A quantitative scenario-based online experiment used a 2 × 2 × 2 between-subjects design with 527 valid respondents. Data were analyzed using three-way factorial ANOVA, confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation modelling, and bootstrap analysis with 5,000 resamples. Early disclosure, high specificity, and stated professional review or oversight produced more favourable evaluations across the disclosure conditions examined. Human control generated the largest main effects on perceived authenticity (partial η² = 0.346), message credibility (partial η² = 0.316), brand trust (partial η² = 0.318), and usage intention (partial η² = 0.166). Perceived authenticity increased brand trust (β = 0.304, p < 0.001), message credibility had a stronger effect on brand trust (β = 0.598, p < 0.001), and brand trust increased usage intention (β = 0.736, p < 0.001). Timing and specificity showed significant indirect effects on brand trust, while human control showed both direct and indirect effects. The effects were predominantly additive, with only a small timing × human-control interaction for message credibility (partial η² = 0.009). These findings indicate that, when AI disclosure is present, timing, specificity, and stated professional oversight provide distinct trust-relev

latest.title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA E AS MUDANÇAS NA DEMANDA POR BENS DE CONHECIMENTO E SERVIÇOS: UMA PERSPECTIVA DA TEORIA DO CONSUMIDOR
latest.abstract: Este artigo examina como a teoria do consumidor pode explicar as mudanças na demanda por bens de conhecimento e serviços provocadas pela difusão da inteligência artificial generativa. Trata-se de ensaio teórico de natureza dedutiva, que articula a literatura de microeconomia e de economia da informação a evidências recentes sobre os efeitos da tecnologia em mercados de serviços cognitivos. Argumenta-se que a IA generativa opera como um choque que reduz o preço relativo e o custo temporal da produção cognitiva padronizada, permitindo distinguir três mecanismos analíticos: o efeito substituição, que pode deslocar a demanda dos serviços humanos padronizados em direção às alternativas automatizadas, conforme a sobreposição de características entre eles; o efeito renda, ligado à mudança do poder de compra monetário, e a economia de tempo, que constitui um mecanismo distinto; e a reordenação da escassez, pela qual o valor migra de atributos tornados abundantes para atenção, confiança e autenticidade. Conclui-se que a demanda pode se recompor entre alternativas automatizadas e serviços humanos, conforme a tarefa, a qualidade e as preferências dos consumidores, e propõe-se uma tipologia analítica de mercados com base na elasticidade-preço cruzada, cujas hipóteses condicionais devem ser testadas empiricamente em pesquisas futuras.

latest.title: Incremental value of wearable digital phenotypes for anxiety under real-world missingness
latest.abstract: Abstract Wearable sensing may enable low-burden digital phenotyping of anxiety, but its incremental value beyond brief symptom questionnaires remains uncertain under real-world missingness. We analyzed a public 4-week dataset from 49 adults with two 14-day participant-windows aligned to week-2 and week-4 GAD-7 assessments (98 windows; 22 with GAD-7 ≥ 5). XGBoost models based on demographic/lifestyle, wearable, questionnaire, and combined feature sets were evaluated by participant-level leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, with uncertainty estimated by participant-level cluster bootstrap. QUESTIONNAIRE models achieved the highest classification performance (AUC 0.888; average precision 0.826; Brier 0.085), whereas WEARABLE alone remained near chance (AUC 0.501). Adding wearables to QUESTIONNAIRE did not improve performance (ΔAUC − 0.045; ΔBrier 0.025). In the high-compliance subset (34 participants; 68 windows), wearable-only discrimination remained weak; questionnaire-plus-wearable point estimates were more favorable, but confidence intervals included the null. Continuous GAD-7 analyses showed improved prediction beyond demographic/lifestyle variables but little added value beyond questionnaires. These findings indicate baseline-dependent incremental value: wearable-derived features may provide adjunctive information when questionnaire data are unavailable or sparse, but their added value was limited once baseline symptom questionnaires were available.

latest.title: Developing Competitive Intelligence Capabilities in MBA Education: A Pedagogical Framework for Strategic Decision-Making in the Age of AI
latest.venue: Journal of Intelligence Studies in Business
latest.abstract: Competitive intelligence (CI) is increasingly important for managerial decision-making amid technological disruption, intensified competition, and environmental uncertainty. Nevertheless, MBA programs rarely teach CI as an integrated managerial capability. Drawing on literature concerning competitive intelligence, dynamic capabilities, experiential learning, strategic foresight, and management education, this conceptual article develops a pedagogical framework for incorporating CI into MBA curricula. The framework comprises four mutually reinforcing capability domains: external awareness, analytical intelligence, strategic foresight, and decision support. It connects these capabilities with appropriate learning objectives, experiential teaching methods, assessment practices, and managerial applications. The article also examines the growing role of artificial intelligence in CI education. It argues that although AI can accelerate information collection, pattern identification, and preliminary analysis, effective intelligence still requires source verification, contextual interpretation, ethical judgment, and managerial accountability. The proposed framework positions CI not as a narrowly specialized information function but as a cross-functional managerial capability connecting environmental sensing with strategic action. By integrating human judgment, AI-enabled analysis, and experiential learning, MBA programs can better prepare managers to recognize consequential change, challenge established assumptions, communicate uncertainty, and make informed strategic decisions.

latest.title: The Effects of Digital HRM Practices, Digital Trust, and Adaptive Leadership on Employee Digital Innovation Behavior in the Banking and Financial Sector
latest.venue: Lead Journal of Economy and Administration
latest.abstract: The aim of this research is to investigate the effect of Digital HRM Practices, Digital Trust and Adaptive Leadership on Employee Digital Innovation Behavior in banking and financial industry in Indonesia. The study applied quantitative method using survey technique on the workers of banking organizations and financial institutions that have used digital technology in their operational operations and human resource management procedures. A purposive sample approach was used and the criteria for respondents were current employees, with a minimum of one (1) year work experience, digital platforms used in work activities and having digital-based human resource management procedures. The data collection was conducted through an online questionnaire sent through Google form. The data analysis used is multiple linear regression. The results show that Digital HRM Practices, Digital Trust and Adaptive Leadership have a positive and significant effect on Employee Digital Innovation Behavior. The findings show the important factors for enhancing employees’ digital creative behavior are the application of digital-based human resource management techniques, the belief in security and dependability of technology, and the role of adaptive leadership. The study offers practical implications for companies to improve digital HRM practices, enhance security and transparency of digital systems and develop an adaptive leadership style that encourages empowerment, collaboration and continuous learning to improve Employee Digital Innovation Behavior.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Digital Information Transparency and Customer Trust in Islamic Banking: A Case Study of BYOND by Bank Syariah Indonesia
latest.abstract: The digital transformation of banking requires information transparency as a key factor in building customer trust. This study aims to identify the transparency of financial transaction information provided through the BYOND by Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI) application and its contribution to customer trust at BSI Padangsidimpuan. This research employs a qualitative approach involving 32 customers selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation, then analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that clear, accurate, complete, and accessible transaction information contributes to strengthening customer trust. Nevertheless, challenges related to application comprehension and internet connectivity remain. This study highlights the strategic role of digital information transparency in strengthening customer trust and supporting the sustainability of Islamic banking services

latest.title: What shared responses reveal about audience behavior: neural prediction and the emerging potential of peripheral synchrony
latest.abstract: Predicting audience responses to dynamic media remains a significant challenge in neuromarketing and neuroforecasting. Intersubject correlation (ISC) has been proposed to address this need by quantifying the temporal similarity of neural, physiological, and behavioral responses among individuals exposed to the same stimulus. This narrative mini-review examines how ISC relates to preferences, judgments, and behavior and proposes a conceptual framework for interpreting its predictive value. Across modalities, ISC consistently reflects shared stimulus processing and is associated with attention, alongside additional links to engagement, memory, and higher-order narrative processing. Neural ISC has shown associations with individual, group, and population-level outcomes, although findings vary by neural modality, analytic approach, and behavioral endpoint. Peripheral ISC derived from gaze, heart rate, electrodermal activity, and facial expressions provides complementary information about interindividual alignment, but direct evidence for predicting consumer outcomes remains limited. At the same time, neural and peripheral measures capture various aspects of shared response dynamics, and combining them in a multimodal ISC approach may help distinguish synchronization in different functional domains, including perceptual, attentional, autonomic, affective, and valuation-related processes, and clarify their relationship to the target outcome. The proposed framework therefore conceptualizes ISC as a probabilistic predictor whose predictive value depends on which functional processes underlie the observed synchrony and their relevance to the specific outcome of interest.

latest.title: Uncovering non-linearities in airline service experience: a dual cognitive-affective evaluation framework
latest.abstract: This study proposes an explainable Machine Learning (ML) approach to unravel the non-linear, asymmetric, and threshold-dependent drivers of air passenger experience. By training parallel eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models paired with Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), this research overcomes the limitations of traditional linear modelling, bridging dual-processing satisfaction theory and explainable AI (XAI) to disentangle analytical cognitive quality assessments from holistic affective emotional states. The findings of the proposed work reveal that service factors act differently across these two psychological domains. While operational factors like punctuality act as rigid hygiene factors for the rational mind, experiential aspects like boarding undergo a behavioural change, scaling as the primary accelerator of affective delight. Furthermore, SHAP interaction matrices identify asymmetric moderation effects driven by passenger expectations across different airline business models. By disentangling cognitive quality from affective delight, this research offers a novel eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework that helps airlines safeguard basic operational services against dissatisfaction while prioritizing key interactions that truly foster passenger delight.

latest.title: A Theory-Informed, Large Language Model-Assisted Competitive Intelligence Process for Assessing Competing Quantum Error-Correction Technologies
latest.venue: Journal of Intelligence Studies in Business
latest.abstract: Emerging deep technologies create a competitive technical intelligence challenge because technical architectures, performance claims, ecosystem arrangements, and prospective markets evolve before stable adoption evidence is available. This article develops and illustrates a theory-informed, large language model (LLM)-assisted competitive intelligence (CI) process for assessing the disruptive potential of the development and commercialization of emerging quantum error-correction technologies. The process translates concepts from disruptive innovation, architectural innovation, value proposition analysis, and disruptive threat assessment into intelligence constructs, evidence questions, sequential prompt functions, source-validation criteria, and monitoring outputs. Perplexity.ai supported document discovery, organization, comparison, and preliminary synthesis; the authors evaluated sources, classified claims, and made all final interpretations. The process is illustrated through a comparative documentary analysis of Nord Quantique’s multimode bosonic quantum error-correction approach and IBM’s transmon, surface-code, and quantum low-density parity-check-oriented approach. The analysis identifies NQ as a documented architectural alternative that seeks to embed error protection within superconducting resonator modes. Its proposed reduction of error-correction overhead provides a plausible mechanism for changing system-resource requirements and deployment conditions. However, the retained evidence does not establish comparative system level advantage, lower total cost, a validated customer segment, a disruptive foothold, adoption, or incumbent displacement. The article contributes a source-disciplined and monitorable LLM-assisted CI process for emerging deep technologies. I

latest.title: External resilience controls as sociotechnical governance: an extension of dynamic capabilities theory under externally driven volatility
latest.venue: Qualitative Research in Organizations and Management An International Journal
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines how organizations construct governance responses to externally driven volatility by embedding external signals into control practices. Focusing on climate exposed agricultural firms, this study extends dynamic capabilities theory (DCT) by developing external resilience controls (ERCs) as a sociotechnical governance construct that illuminates how firms make volatility actionable through formal control routines. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a pragmatic constructivist design science orientation, this study combines six years of financial and operational context (2019–2024) with a longitudinal interpretive content analysis of annual report and sustainability disclosures (2022–2024) from five major agricultural firms. An interpretive design approach enables the systematic synthesis of disclosed organizational practices into a conceptual framework. Findings ERCs emerge as sociotechnical governance arrangements that translate external volatility into organizationally meaningful routines and actionable dynamic capabilities. These arrangements materialize through digital sensing infrastructures, traceability systems, scenario thresholds and board-level oversight that collectively shape how firms interpret and respond to climate anomalies, regulatory shifts and technological change. ERCs reveal resilience as an ongoing process of constructing, stabilizing and legitimizing responses to external volatility. Practical implications ERCs offer practitioners an analytic framework to operationalize dynamic capabilities by integrating digital tools and governance structures. They show how firms convert external volatility into actionable sensing, seizing and reconfiguring routines, enabling adaptive decision-making without relying on rigid control mech

latest.title: Institutionalizing Corporate Intelligence in Global Shipping: An AHP-Based Framework for Competitive Intelligence and Counterintelligence
latest.venue: Journal of Intelligence Studies in Business
latest.abstract: In the current dynamic threat landscape, the shipping industry is becoming increasingly exposed to disinformation, espionage, and various security and digital risks. This paper utilizes the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) to present a structured multi-criteria decision-making methodology for the world-class shipping companies to enhance intelligence operations, drawing primary data from eighteen (18) semi-structured interviews with senior leaders, security and compliance professionals from world-class global shipping companies and state intelligence agencies about current gaps and organizational needs. Utilizing systematic research, the results provide a viable structure to allow shipping to reorganize the business model, clarify the business roles, simplify the process of managing intelligence, and leverage sophisticated technology platforms. The main objective is to enhance Competitive Intelligence and Counterintelligence industry wide. The methodology also promotes the use of human and open-source intelligence, anticipates threats, mitigates risks, and raises internal awareness about Counterintelligence. It calls for shipping to align its intelligence functions with the broader geopolitical context of digital transformation. Ultimately, this paper endeavors to equip maritime actors with new and adaptive intelligence competences and enter a broader discussion at the junction of sectors around resilience and proactive security in an increasingly complex global environment.

latest.title: How recommendation explanation cues shape consumers’ multistage online behavior: An integrative information-processing framework
latest.abstract: 摘要： 算法推荐已成为电商平台影响消费者决策的重要信息环境, 但既有研究侧重算法类型、准确性及转化效果, 较少考察推荐解释线索对消费者信息加工与多阶段决策的影响。本文聚焦前端的相似用户型与产品属性型解释线索, 将其视为具有不同心理含义的信息线索, 而非后台算法类型: 前者强调相似他人行为, 后者强调产品属性匹配, 并构建购前搜索—购中选择—购后反馈框架。购前, 产品属性型线索通过降低感知产品差异促进目标导向型搜索; 相似用户型线索通过提高感知产品差异促进探索型搜索。购中, 相似用户型线索借助社会证明降低感知产品不确定性, 提高选择不熟悉产品的可能性, 增强选择信心并提升决策效率。购后, 相似用户型线索形成的推荐来源表征通过增强产品社会联结感, 提高反馈努力与质量, 并可能在后续评价触点中被重新激活。本文揭示推荐解释线索通过差异化信息加工机制影响消费者在线多阶段行为, 为推荐解释设计与消费者信息加工研究提供整合框架。

latest.title: Sustaining Mechanism for the Competitive Advantage of Alphabet: Synergy between Business Model and Corporate Culture
latest.abstract: Another paper identified Berkshire Hathaway’s high concentration in Alphabet Inc. and proved that the investment complies with classical value investment principles. One question has been left open in that paper: what creates and recreates those barriers? This paper will take a step further from an outside investor’s perspective to the firm’s internal mechanisms of sustaining those barriers. First, we will break down the two-sided monetization strategy of Alphabet, its cash flows, and the lock-in that occurs due to Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, and Maps products. Secondly, we will look at engineer-led governance and innovation incentivizing mechanism, such as 20% time and internal incubating, as well as the talent flywheel that is funded by $49.3 billion of research spendings in 2024. The key argument that we make here is that the moat that Alphabet has is bidirectional synergies: the business model generates the cash flows which fuel cultural innovation while the culture supports the algorithms and products that guarantee monetization. We will test our hypothesis dialectically through bureaucracy, regulation pressures, and capital costs of artificial intelligence transformation. Ultimately, this study provides a comprehensive framework for understanding how technological giants maintain their competitive edge in a rapidly evolving digital landscape, offering valuable insights for both academic researchers and industry practitioners navigating complex market dynamics.

latest.title: Beyond Personalization: The Paradox of Trust, Consumer Autonomy and Engagement in AI-Driven Interactive Digital Media
latest.venue: Journal of Art Design and Creative Media
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed digital and interactive media by enabling personalized content, algorithmic recommendations and increasingly responsive consumer experiences. Although these developments offer opportunities to improve relevance, convenience and engagement, they also raise important questions concerning privacy, consumer autonomy and trust. Existing discussions frequently emphasize the benefits of personalization and the effectiveness of digital engagement, yet these perspectives may overlook the possibility that the same technological features that enhance consumer experiences can also generate perceptions of surveillance, manipulation and loss of control. This conceptual article examines the dual nature of AI-driven interactive digital media through an integration of the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, Privacy Calculus Theory and Psychological Reactance Theory. The article proposes a conceptual framework in which personalization, perceived interactivity and algorithmic transparency influence consumer responses through two interconnected pathways: a value-creation pathway associated with perceived relevance, trust and engagement, and a resistance pathway associated with privacy concerns, perceived manipulation and psychological reactance. Consumer autonomy is further considered as an important boundary condition shaping these relationships. The proposed framework contributes to digital marketing and interactive media scholarship by conceptualizing consumer engagement as a conditional outcome rather than an inherently positive consequence of technological sophistication. The article also offers implications for digital marketers, platform designers and policymakers seeking to develop more transparent, trustworthy and consumer-centred dig

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Abstract Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Impact of digital transformation on SME’s marketing performance: role of social media and market turbulence
hot.abstract: Despite the rising relevance of digital transformation, there is still a knowledge vacuum due to limited literature available on digital transformation.
