latest.title: Destructive Leadership: The Hidden Cost To People And Organizations
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Destructive leadership represents a significant organizational phenomenon whose consequences extend beyond the immediate interaction between leaders and employees and may exert a sustained influence on organizational climate and culture. This article examines the mechanisms through which destructive leadership behaviours manifest at the organizational level, with particular emphasis on changes in communication, trust and perceived fairness, role clarity, workload, recognition systems, and the gradual establishment of dysfunctional norms and behavioural patterns. Organizational climate and organizational culture are analysed as interrelated but conceptually distinct levels through which the consequences of destructive leadership can be identified. Finally, the article discusses practical approaches to the early recognition, prevention, and mitigation of its impact on employees and organizations.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: The Monitoring Paradox: Why Oversight Mechanisms Fail to Predict PPP Infrastructure Projects Performance in Kenya
latest.abstract: Purpose: The study explored role of project monitoring mechanisms in enhancing performance of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure projects in Kenya. Policy puts a lot of emphasis on the need for monitoring along the project lifecycle; however, many PPP projects continue to display inefficiencies pointing towards weak monitoring systems. Materials and Methods: Data were collected from 252 respondents representing government agencies, private consortia, and project management units across 103 PPP projects. Regression analysis was used to test relationship between project monitoring mechanisms and project performance. Findings: Project monitoring had a statistically significant but weak positive influence on project performance (β = .014, p < .005). The positive but not so profound effect suggests that the monitoring frameworks that exists are largely compliance-oriented rather than the one that drives performance in the project environment. Implications to Theory, Practice and Policy: The study recommends institutionalizing real-time monitoring, feedback systems, and adoption of digital data tools to strengthen accountability within PPP infrastructure projects in Kenya. To anchor these measures, the Public Private Partnerships Act, 2021 and the regulations around privately funded public infrastructure should be amended to create a performance-based monitoring making it mandatory. This includes standardization of KPIs, periodic independent performance reviews, and public disclosure of monitoring reports across the project lifecycle. Keywords: Monitoring Mechanisms, PPP, Infrastructure Performance, Project Governance, Kenya

latest.title: The Influence of Profitability, Interest Rates (BI Rate) and Institutional Ownership on Stock Returns at PT Akasha Wira Internasional Tbk
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationships between profitability, the Bank Indonesia policy interest rate, institutional ownership, and stock returns at PT Akasha Wira International Tbk over the 2013–2024 period. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data obtained from the company’s annual reports and Bank Indonesia publications. The dataset comprises 12 annual observations. Profitability was measured using return on assets (ROA), while institutional ownership was measured by the proportion of shares held by institutional investors. The interest-rate variable was based on Bank Indonesia’s published policy-rate series, taking into account changes in the official benchmark terminology during the observation period. Multiple linear regression and hypothesis testing were conducted using SPSS version 23. The results indicate that profitability is positively and significantly associated with stock returns (t = 4.476, p = 0.002), whereas the policy interest rate is negatively and significantly associated with stock returns (t = −2.830, p = 0.022). Institutional ownership does not exhibit a statistically significant partial association with stock returns (t = 1.803, p = 0.109). Simultaneously, the three independent variables are statistically significant in the regression model (F = 10.610, p = 0.004). The model yields an R-squared of 0.799, indicating that the predictors jointly account for 79.9% of the in-sample variation in stock returns, while the adjusted R-squared is 0.724 after accounting for the number of predictors and observations. Given the limited sample and single-company setting, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. This study provides case-specific evidence concerning the relationships between firm-level profitability, monetary policy, owner

latest.title: The Effect of Campus Image and Word of Mouth on Students' Decisions in Choosing a Business Education Study Program at State University Of Medan
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Ekonomi, Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of campus image and word of mouth on the decision of 2025 cohort students in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Universitas Negeri Medan. This research employed a quantitative approach using an ex post facto method. The population consisted of 111 students, all of whom were selected as the sample through the total sampling technique. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression, t-test, F-test, and the coefficient of determination (R²). The results showed that campus image had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (t value = 7.322; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Word of mouth also had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (t value = 5.779; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). Simultaneously, both variables had a positive and significant influence on students' decisions in choosing the Business Education Study Program at Medan State University (f value = 40.939; sig = 0.000 < 0.05). The findings indicate that 43.1% of the variation in students' decisions to choose the Business Education Study Program can be explained by campus image and word of mouth, while the remaining 56.9% is influenced by other factors outside the scope of this study.

latest.title: A qualitative assessment of perceived resilience in agricultural marketing cooperatives
latest.venue: Journal of Co-operative Organization and Management
latest.abstract: Agricultural marketing cooperatives are vital to agricultural systems, yet their resilience remains understudied. This research applies and extends the resilience assessment framework for farm systems to these cooperatives, examining robustness, adaptability, transformability, and anticipation. Using a qualitative approach, we conducted in-depth interviews with 18 German cooperative decision-makers from December 2023 to February 2024 to examine their perceptions of resilience. Our study employs thematic analysis and deductive category formation to investigate the framework's applicability, gain insights into perceived resilience capacities and strategies, and examine how cooperative values are perceived to foster resilience through the resilience capacities. Results show the adapted framework effectively captures unique cooperative aspects from the perspective of interviewees. Respondents generally describe their organizations as robust and diversified, and as maintaining resilience through adaptability in business fields and functions. While overall resilience is perceived as high, individual capacities vary, with robustness rated highest and anticipatory capacity lowest. Cooperative values are viewed by respondents as contributing to resilience, especially during crises, but are also described as facing challenges. This study provides one of the first systematic qualitative analyses of perceived resilience in agricultural marketing cooperatives and contributes to understanding factors that may support stability and sustainability in food systems.

latest.title: Exploring adverse childhood experiences in healthcare professional students: insights from a mixed-methods pilot study
latest.abstract: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are associated with long-term mental and physical health outcomes and may influence vulnerability to stress and burnout. Despite growing attention to clinician well-being, limited empirical research has examined ACE prevalence among healthcare professional (HCP) students or how early adversity may shape training experiences. This mixed-methods pilot study assessed ACE prevalence and demographic associations among HCP students and explored students’ perceptions of how ACEs influence well-being and professional development. One hundred and fifty students from medicine, nursing, occupational therapy, physician assistant, and physical therapy programs at a private research university in the United States participated in the survey. Participants completed an online survey including sociodemographic items and the ACE questionnaire. Descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression were used to examine prevalence and associations of ACE scores. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with eight students and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Overall, 83.3% of participants reported at least one ACE and 32% reported four or more. Mean ACE score was 2.80 (SD = 2.28). Nursing students reported significantly higher ACE scores than medical students (B = 1.19, p = .006). In analyses of race, participants identifying as Black or African American, Asian, or another race were combined because of small subgroup sizes and reported higher ACE scores than White participants (B = 0.92, p = .016). Age and gender were not significant predictors. The most frequently reported ACEs were verbal abuse (53.3%), living with a household member with mental illness (45.3%), and physical abuse (35.3%). Qualitative findings indicated that students percei

latest.title: Extending reach while maintaining oversight: Clinicians' perspectives on digital mental health implementation in youth services
latest.abstract: Background Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) offer a promising means of extending care for children and adolescents, yet their integration into routine clinical services remains inconsistent. The implementation conditions clinicians identify as prerequisites for adoption carry greater relevance given the emergence of AI tools now being used by young people. This study examined the perspectives of mental health professionals (MHPs) working with children and young people to identify key implementation considerations for the development and adoption of DMHIs. Methods Nineteen focus groups were conducted with 50 mental health clinicians from a range of service settings in Queensland, Australia between May 2020 and May 2021. Data were analyzed using a mixed deductive-inductive thematic approach informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Results MHPs were cautiously optimistic about DMHIs, viewing them as most valuable when implemented as supplementary rather than replacement tools. Key perceived uses included waitlist support, screening and assessment, between-session engagement, and flexible treatment pathways. However, MHPs consistently emphasized the need to preserve clinical judgement and oversight across all stages of DMHI use. Risk management, duty of care, and privacy and confidentiality were identified as critical prerequisites for implementation. Conclusions Successful DMHI implementation in child and adolescent mental health services requires flexible, clinician-centered integration approaches, robust risk management protocols, and clear organizational frameworks delineating clinician responsibility. As AI tools are adopted by young people largely outside clinical oversight, these findings offer a grounded baseline for eval
keywords: child and adolescent mental health services

latest.title: Family environment, health risk behaviors, and mental health among chinese five-year vocational education students: a cross-sectional network analysis
latest.abstract: Mental health problems, particularly depression and anxiety, pose a global public health challenge. Vocational education students are an understudied population, and the complex interrelationships among family environment, health risk behaviors, and psychological symptoms remain unclear. This study employed network analysis to examine these associations, aiming to identify central symptoms and potential gender differences. A total of 1,601 students enrolled in five-year higher vocational education programs were recruited from two vocational colleges in Nanning, Guangxi, using multistage cluster random sampling. Participants were aged 12–23 years, representing late adolescence and emerging adulthood. Family environment, health risk behaviors, and mental health status were assessed using the Family Environment Scale, the Student Health Status and Influencing Factors Questionnaire, and the Mental Health Scale for Middle School Students, respectively. The EBICglasso method was used to estimate networks and derive centrality indices, followed by the Network Comparison Test to evaluate gender differences. “Depression” and “Anxiety” showed the highest strength centrality. Family “Cohesion” and “Conflict” showed the highest bridge strength across domains. The relatively strongest edge was observed between “Sleep deprivation” and “Depression.” No significant gender differences were detected in network structure or global strength. Depression and anxiety were the most central symptoms in this network. Family cohesion and sleep deprivation were statistically prominent bridge nodes and may represent promising targets for future intervention research. Family-based emotional communication training and sleep health promotion warrant further investigation.

latest.title: Day-to-Day Variation in Perceived Causal Networks: A Feasibility Study in Two Psychiatric Settings
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose The network approach conceptualizes psychopathology as a system of causally interacting problems of living. Longitudinal Perceived Causal Networks (L-PECAN) is a self-report method designed to capture day-to-day variability in patients’ perceived causal relations between problems. We examined the feasibility of an L-PECAN procedure in two clinical settings and explored within-person variability in perceived causal network structures. Methods Patients in two psychiatric clinics first completed an L-PECAN training week using a generic item list. Personalized items, including contextual factors, were then formulated and used subsequently for a minimum of three weeks. Feasibility was evaluated via recruitment rates and adherence. Within-person variability was examined using saturation and drift analyses. Results Eight patients completed the protocol. Median daily completion times ranged from one to eight minutes. Participants largely perceived their personalized problems as being caused by their other problems. Some causal relations were perceived consistently across days, but overall network structures showed substantial day-to-day variability. Conclusions An L-PECAN procedure incorporating a training week and personalized nodes appeared feasible in the university clinic, whereas uptake and adherence indicated greater implementation challenges in specialist psychiatric care. The method provides a structured way to examine day-to-day variability in perceived causal problem networks. Further research is needed to establish feasibility across clinical populations and to evaluate validity and clinical utility.

latest.title: Social capital and ambidextrous leadership as drivers of sustainable competitive advantage in export SMEs: The mediating roles of knowledge management and innovation capability -- evidence from Bali, Indonesia
latest.abstract: This study investigates how social capital and ambidextrous leadership contribute to sustainable competitive advantage in export-oriented small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) by examining the mediating roles of knowledge management and innovation capability and assessing business performance as an additional pathway. Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities perspective, survey data were collected from 114 export-oriented SMEs in Bali, Indonesia, and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The results show that social capital and ambidextrous leadership both positively influence knowledge management, which in turn enhances innovation capability. Innovation capability has a significant positive effect on both business performance and sustainable competitive advantage, whereas business performance does not significantly predict sustainable competitive advantage. The mediation results further indicate that knowledge management mediates the effects of social capital and ambidextrous leadership on innovation capability. In addition, the serial mediation pathway from ambidextrous leadership to sustainable competitive advantage through knowledge management and innovation capability is significant, whereas the corresponding pathway from social capital is not. These findings suggest that sustainable competitive advantage in export-oriented SMEs is shaped more by capability development than by short-term performance outcomes and that leadership plays a critical role in converting relational resources into sustained strategic value. The study contributes to strategic management research by clarifying the mechanisms through which relational and managerial resources are transformed into long-term competitiveness in dynamic export mar

latest.title: Older adults’ acceptance of robot-led rehabilitative exercise
latest.abstract: Abstract An aging global population has increased the demand for physical therapists and caregivers. Assistive robots may help address this rising demand, but there are mixed results regarding their acceptance. The Zesty Exercise System for Therapeutic Engagement (ZEST-E), a custom-programmed Hello Robot Stretch RE1 mobile manipulator, was previously evaluated with people with Parkinson’s disease and with exercise specialists. In this exploratory, mixed-methods study, 21 community-dwelling older adults (CDOAs) (aged 65–85 years) completed a single supervised session of six robot-led exercises, standardized surveys, and a semi-structured interview to assess their reception of ZEST-E. Median ratings on 5-point scales, where 5 is the most positive, were 4.00 for Perceived Usefulness, Attitude, Intent to Use, and Perceived Enjoyment, and 3.67 for Perceived Ease of Use. Median psychosocial-impact scores were modestly positive (0.88–1.00 on a $$-3$$ to +3 scale), and median NASA-TLX ratings on 5-point scales indicated moderate Physical Demand (3.00) and low Frustration (1.00). In interviews, 16 participants (76%) described ZEST-E as engaging, whereas statements about using it in daily life were nearly balanced (12 positive vs. 11 negative). Initial impressions were, therefore, favorable, but perceived willingness to use ZEST-E independently was conditional. The principal proposed improvements include improving communication and guidance, providing a personalized exercise experience, and simplifying setup and configuration to improve independent usability. These findings seek to inform the development of ZEST-E and other similar interactive robotic systems beyond limited trials in research clinics.

latest.title: From Fragmented Assets to a Coordinated Destination: A Governance and Gap Analysis of Tourism Development in Cape Coast, Ghana
latest.abstract: Cape Coast, Ghana, has substantial heritage, coastal, cultural, and educational assets, yet visitor activity remains concentrated at Cape Coast Castle, where recorded visits rose from 101,134 in 2023 to 141,523 in 2025. This study examines how these assets are governed and where the links between them break down. A qualitative, multi-source design combined policy documents, in-depth interviews with 26 tourists, a tourism resource assessment, and an exploratory review of the city’s sister cities (Bonn, Little Rock and New Orleans). Arnstein’s ladder of participation served as the diagnostic framework, supported by an analysis of the sources of stakeholder influence. Interviews were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, and draft findings were discussed with 32 stakeholders at a consultative workshop. Empirical findings comprised eight recurring gaps, including weak institutional coordination, limited visitor services and information, narrow product diversification, and limited community participation. From the lens of Arnstein’s ladder of participation, residents and small businesses appear mainly as consultees rather than shared decision-makers, a pattern interpreted here as policy invisibility, a descriptive concept rather than a new theory. The findings are perceptual and non-generalizable, and the sister-city material offers ideas rather than transferable models. Separately from these findings, the paper recommends a phased, indicative framework aligned with the Eight-Year Development Plan (2026–2033), pending baseline measurement. The paper argues that Cape Coast’s central task is coordination across institutions and districts rather than adding attractions. The contribution is empirical and applied: a diagnostic account of destination governance in a secondar

latest.title: AN ANALYSIS OF FACTORS INFLUENCING SUSTAINABLE CONSUMPTION BEHAVIORS AMONG GENERATION Z IN KAZAKHSTAN
latest.abstract: This study explores the attitudes and behaviors of Generation Z in Kazakhstan toward sustainable consumption and considers implications for marketers seeking to engage this environmentally conscious demographic. Drawing on a survey of 329 university students, the research examines factors influencing Gen Z’s sustainable behaviors, including environmental concern, social influence, and perceptions of sustainable product pricing. The results reveal a significant positive correlation between environmental concern and engagement in sustainable practices, indicating that Gen Z shows a preference for eco-friendly products and brands committed to sustainability. Given the higher prices of eco-friendly options, pricing remains an important consideration in Gen Z’s sustainable purchasing decisions. Findings emphasize the importance of transparent communication and authentic sustainability practices in building trust and loyalty with this demographic. Marketers should align their strategies with Gen Z’s values by adopting pricing approaches that support eco-friendly choices and leveraging social media to foster communities of conscious consumers.

latest.title: KAZLEATHER 2030: A POLICY FRAMEWORK FOR TRANSFORMING KAZAKHSTAN’S LEATHER INDUSTRY
latest.abstract: The article considers the development of the leather industry of Kazakhstan in the context of industry diversification and sustainable production. The goal of the research is to assess the current state of the leather industry and develop policyoriented recommendations to transform it into a competitive and environmentally sustainable industry. The methodology uses a mixed-methods approach that includes analysis of official statistical data, policy analysis, and semi-structured interviews with key industry actors. The findings indicate that the industry is characterized by limited deep processing, underutilized capacity, environmental costs, weak institutional coordination, and a shortage of personnel. Based on the comparative analysis of the European Union, Türkiye, China, and Uzbekistan, a framework concept for the KazLeather 2030 transformation is proposed that includes the e-vet&Traceability digital platform, the KazLeather Research Grant and the implementation of the KazLeather environmental standard. The research contributes to discussions on modernizing resource-based industries and offers practical instruments for upgrading value-added chains.

latest.title: Impact of Frauds and Corruption on Public Procurement in Nigeria
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science Humanity & Management Research
latest.abstract: The study assessed the Impact of Frauds and Corruption on Public Procurement in Nigeria; and dispassionately determined whether or not the common forms and techniques of fraud and corruption have significant effect on public procurement system in Nigeria. The study assessed procurement corruption using long datasets (1999-2024) from recognised secondary sources including Transparency International’s Corruption Perception Index (CPI) scores, Global Competitiveness Reports, and reports from local anti-corruption agencies. Findings show Nigeria’s CPI scores ranged from 10 to 28, reflecting persistently high perceived corruption. The study concluded that procurement corruption in Nigeria is not merely a product of individual misconduct but a reflection of deeper institutional dysfunction, aiding fraud and corruption to undermine public procurement. It therefore, recommends full digitization of processes integrated with open contracting data standards that include compulsory use of NOCOPO by the Federal and State MDAs. To ensure accountability and transparency of public procurement in Nigeria, real-time bidding and contract data must be published in line with Public Procurement Act of 2007.

latest.title: Insights from Industry: A Contextualised Analysis of How Tertiary Accounting Programmes Can Be Redesigned in the Age Of AI
latest.abstract: This study examines how artificial intelligence is transforming graduate training in Irish accounting firms and resulting implications for tertiary accounting education. Through qualitative interviews with representatives from top-tier, upper mid-tier, and lower mid-tier firms, the research identifies significant variation in AI adoption across the profession, with larger firms implementing advanced integration while smaller practices adopt more incremental approaches. The findings reveal that entry-level routine tasks are increasingly automated, requiring graduates to develop earlier competency in supervisory, analytical, and governance roles. The study identifies that differing levels of AI integration across firm tiers create unequal graduate exposure, raising concerns about potential inequalities in professional development. Drawing on these findings and Ireland's Higher Education Authority National Policy Framework on Generative AI in Teaching and Learning, the study proposes an AI Impact Response Model for Tertiary-Level Accounting Programmes. This model emphasises three core competencies: digital skills, discipline-specific knowledge, and diagnostic and communication capabilities, delivered through spiral curriculum design across all programme modules, content and assessments. The recommendations provide accounting educators with practical guidance for preparing graduates who can operate effectively across diverse practice environments whilst preserving the professional judgement and ethical oversight central to the accounting profession.

latest.title: Internet-delivered self-help acceptance and commitment therapy for family carers of people with dementia (iACT4CARERS): a mixed-methods process evaluation of reach and recruitment.
latest.abstract: OBJECTIVES: A mixed-methods process evaluation was conducted alongside a randomised controlled trial of iACT4CARERS, an eight-session, online, self-help Acceptance and Commitment Therapy intervention with minimal therapist support for family carers of people with dementia. The study examined the reach of the intervention and factors influencing recruitment to inform equitable implementation. METHODS: Demographic data from 565 screened carers and interviews with 30 referrers across UK health services were analysed. RESULTS: The screened sample was predominantly aged 50-79 years (82.5%), female (77%), and White (91.7%). Five themes were identified: referrers' coordinated referrals, mutual motivation, and community outreach supported engagement; referrers' trust-building, tailored communication, and timely approaches facilitated participation; carers' time constraints and referrers' assumptions about older carers' digital skills influenced recruitment; proactive outreach was important for engaging ethnic minority carers; and cultural perceptions of mental health created barriers to participation. CONCLUSIONS: The sample was broadly comparable with previous estimates of the UK dementia carer population. For the equitable implementation of interventions such as iACT4CARERS, coordinated recruitment across health, social care, and voluntary organisations, alongside centralised intervention delivery, may be critical. Outreach can be further strengthened by enhancing referrers' communication and empowerment skills, including challenging assumptions about older carers' digital abilities.

latest.title: Analisis Kredibilitas Konten Instagram Terhadap Kepercayaan Calon Jamaah Milenial dalam Perumusan Strategi Konten (Studi Kasus PT An-Nahl Umrah dan Haji)
latest.abstract: Increasing number of Umrah and Hajj pilgrims, where the tight competition among travel agencies in the digital era, and the rise of travel agency fraud cases through social media have created a crisis in the level of trust of prospective pilgrims, especially millennials as active Instagram users. This study aims to analyze the influence of the credibility of Instagram content on the trust of prospective millennial pilgrims in order to provide content strategy recommendations for PT An-Nahl Umrah and Hajj. This study uses a quantitative approach with a survey method. The sampling technique in this study use purposive sampling with 75 respondents. Data were collected through a Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using validity, reliability, classical assumptions and multiple linear regression through the SPSS 26 program. The analysis shows that simultaneously, the three indicators have significant influence on trust, with an F value of 34.193, and partially only the trustworthiness indicator has a dominant influence on trust of β = 0.598, while expertise and attractiveness partially do not have a significant influence on trust. From the results of this study it can be concluded that transparency, honesty and accuracy of information such as testimonial content are the main factors in building trust among prospective millennial pilgrims.

latest.title: Internet-delivered self-help acceptance and commitment therapy for family carers of people with dementia (iACT4CARERS): a mixed-methods process evaluation of reach and recruitment
latest.abstract: Objectives A mixed-methods process evaluation was conducted alongside a randomised controlled trial of iACT4CARERS, an eight-session, online, self-help Acceptance and Commitment Therapy intervention with minimal therapist support for family carers of people with dementia. The study examined the reach of the intervention and factors influencing recruitment to inform equitable implementation.Methods Demographic data from 565 screened carers and interviews with 30 referrers across UK health services were analysed.Results The screened sample was predominantly aged 50–79 years (82.5%), female (77%), and White (91.7%). Five themes were identified: referrers’ coordinated referrals, mutual motivation, and community outreach supported engagement; referrers’ trust-building, tailored communication, and timely approaches facilitated participation; carers’ time constraints and referrers’ assumptions about older carers’ digital skills influenced recruitment; proactive outreach was important for engaging ethnic minority carers; and cultural perceptions of mental health created barriers to participation.Conclusions The sample was broadly comparable with previous estimates of the UK dementia carer population. For the equitable implementation of interventions such as iACT4CARERS, coordinated recruitment across health, social care, and voluntary organisations, alongside centralised intervention delivery, may be critical. Outreach can be further strengthened by enhancing referrers’ communication and empowerment skills, including challenging assumptions about older carers’ digital abilities.

latest.title: Prospective memory deficit associated with major depressive disorder: Causality, clinical impact, and potential molecular mechanisms
latest.abstract: Prospective memory (PM) impairment is frequently observed in major depressive disorder (MDD), yet its causal relationship, clinical impact, and molecular mechanisms remain unclear. To clarify causality between MDD and PM deficits, bidirectional mendelian randomization (MR) was conducted (MDD: n = 1639572; PM deficits: n = 152605). Genetic liability to MDD significantly increased the risk of PM deficits (OR = 1.045, P < 1 × 10 −4 ), with a lack of evidence supporting a reverse causal effect. To assess clinical impact, we recruited 222 patients with MDD and 200 healthy controls (HCs). Patients with MDD showed significantly poorer PM performance across nearly all MIST subscales ( P Bonferroni < 0.05). Among 134 patients with follow-up, linear mixed-effects models revealed slower HAMD reduction in patients with PM deficits ( z = 2.287, P = 0.022). PM performance showed no significant change after treatment ( P = 0.117). To investigate potential mechanisms and therapeutics, shared targets for MDD and PM were identified through network pharmacology and summary-data-based MR, revealing Rap1 signaling as the top enriched pathway with eight core targets. Molecular docking showed relatively weak predicted affinities (mean > −7.5 kcal/mol) of commonly used antidepressants to these targets. Virtual screening of psychiatric compounds identified Hypericin, with strong affinity to the core targets (mean −9.06 kcal/mol). In conclusion, MDD may increase the risk of PM deficits, which are associated with poorer treatment response and show limited improvement following current antidepressant treatments. Rap1-related mechanisms may be involved, and Hypericin may be considered a compound for further investigation.

latest.title: Pengaruh Mikrotransaksi Game Online terhadap Pengelolaan Keuangan Mahasiswa (Survei pada Mahasiswa Jurusan Akuntansi Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Universitas Halu Oleo)
latest.venue: Jurnal Semesta Ilmu Manajemen dan Ekonomi
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh mikrotransaksi game online terhadap pengelolaan keuangan mahasiswa Jurusan Akuntansi Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Universitas Halu Oleo. Populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah mahasiswa Jurusan Akuntansi Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Universitas Halu Oleo angkatan 2022–2025. Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan metode purposive sampling, sehingga diperoleh 90 responden. Jenis data yang digunakan adalah data kuantitatif dengan sumber data primer yang diperoleh melalui penyebaran kuesioner. Metode analisis data menggunakan regresi linear sederhana dengan bantuan software IBM SPSS versi 31. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa mikrotransaksi game online berpengaruh negatif terhadap pengelolaan keuangan mahasiswa. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa semakin tinggi intensitas mahasiswa dalam melakukan mikrotransaksi, maka kemampuan mereka dalam mengelola keuangan cenderung menurun. Berdasarkan hasil penelitian dapat disimpulkan bahwa mikrotransaksi memiliki pengaruh negatif terhadap pengelolaan keuangan mahasiswa, sehingga mahasiswa disarankan untuk mampu meningkatkan pengendalian keuangan, khususnya dalam pengeluaran pada mikrotransaksi game online.

latest.title: The Influence of Collectivist Culture on Senior High School Students’ Cognition of Cyberbullying
latest.abstract: Cyberbullying has been an emerging problem among high schoolers and is increasing in rate with the wide use of the internet, and its negative effect on individual mental health. In this study, the researcher aims to explore the impact of collectivist culture to the high school students’ perception of cyberbullying by using a survey that led to 324 valid respondents. The findings show that the collectivist cultural values have a significant effect on High School students as most students consider cyberbullying as an irrational emotional release, anti-social and legally outlawed. In this type of culture, pursuing group harmony may be a cultural incentive for not challenging and confronting others openly, but students still consider that online aggression does result in harm. Based on the research results, this study recommends two policies: First, the need to increase the education of students’ cultural literacy so that students can harmonize with their groups and also be responsible as individuals in dealing with cyberbullying; and secondly, strengthening the reporting system and supporting students in school to be able to report so as to minimize refusal in action in the event of cyberbullying to prevent students from being silenced by peer pressure that can lead to dangerous responses. Studies like this one inform theoretical frameworks for intervening in the context of school bullying and give practical suggestions for culturally-responsive intervention strategies in collectivist contexts.

latest.title: Analysis of HR Administration Implementation in Workload Management and Work Communication in the Rooms Department Division of Anara Sky Kualanamu Hotel
latest.venue: International Journal of Management Research and Economics
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of Human Resources (HR) administration regarding workload management and workplace communication within the Rooms Division of Anara Sky Kualanamu Hotel. The study is contextualized by the dynamic operational nature of the hotel industry-specifically within the Rooms Division, which faces fluctuating workloads due to changes in occupancy rates, guest service requirements, and work schedules. Furthermore, effective workplace communication is crucial for supporting staff coordination and operational smoothness. Poorly managed workloads and ineffective communication can lead to misunderstandings, hinder coordination, and potentially impact service quality. This study employs a qualitative method with a descriptive approach. Informants were selected using purposive sampling, involving individuals with direct knowledge and experience regarding HR administration, workload management, and workplace communication within the Rooms Division. Data collection was conducted through interviews, observation, and documentation. A qualitative approach was utilized to gain an in-depth understanding of HR administration practices, as well as the informants' experiences and perceptions regarding actual working conditions.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: The Interplay of Digital and Physical Materialities in IT Affordances: A Study of Governance of Controlled Medications in a Hospital
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT In studies of information technology (IT) in organizations, affordance theory may be used to explain what possibilities for action IT offers, under what conditions they are actualized and how they shape action and outcomes. Affordance theory suggests that materiality matters because it furnishes possibilities for action. However, in studies of IT affordances, the digital and physical materialities of IT are usually in focus, while the physical materiality of non‐IT artefacts is seldom considered. This paper examines how the physical materiality of non‐IT artefacts conditions the action possibilities an IT system offers its users. We base our observations on a study of IT implemented in a hospital to improve visibility and accountability of the use of controlled drugs, such as opioids. We compare how the materiality of both IT and paper‐based systems used for these purposes interplays with the materiality of the medications and other non‐IT artefacts in nurses and pharmacists' accountability work. We found different combinations of technologies and medications, condition visibility for the organization in different ways, with distinct ways of knowing about medication work, and different potential accountability outcomes. Temporal processes of accountability work, such as recurrence, accumulation or temporal lag, also condition different outcomes of affordance actualization. Overall, by illuminating material and temporal influences behind visibility and potential for accountability afforded by IT to organizations we deepen the understanding of the action potential afforded by IT and reveal opportunities for redesign of technology and organizational processes.

latest.title: Internet use for learning and insomnia symptoms among high school and university students in China: a two-wave network analysis
latest.abstract: Background Insomnia symptoms and internet use are both common among adolescents, but existing studies often rely on broad measures of screen exposure or global sleep outcomes. It remains unclear whether specific internet-use activities are associated with individual insomnia symptoms and whether these associations differ by educational context. This study aims to explore the association between internet use activity and insomnia symptoms among Chinese high school and university students. Methods Two-wave prospective longitudinal data were collected between 2024 and 2025 from high school and university students in Sichuan and Chongqing, China. Six internet-use activities were assessed: communication, entertainment, gaming, shopping, self-directed learning, and browsing/news use. Insomnia symptoms were measured with the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). Longitudinal models were then fitted in the full sample and stratified by high school and university students. Residualised longitudinal networks were compared between high school and university students. Results Among 4226 students (age: 18.34 ± 1.33, 62.3% female), gaming was positively associated with five ISI items at baseline, whereas self-directed learning was negatively associated with the same items at baseline. Follow-up cross-sectional associations were similar but weaker. No association between Internet-use activities and insomnia symptoms was retained in pooled longitudinal models after Holm adjustment. Four associations were retained among high school students, whereas none was retained among university students. Conclusions Internet-use activities showed different cross-sectional associations and longitudinal associations at item level with insomnia symptoms. Future research should consider activity type and edu

latest.title: REVIEW EFFECTIVENESS IN GENERATIVE AI-ASSISTED SUSTAINABILITY REPORTING: A CONCEPTUAL ANALYSIS OF DECOUPLING AND ORGANIZATIONAL ACCOUNTABILITY
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support the drafting and revision of sustainability reports, but the existence of human review procedures does not necessarily improve disclosure quality. Drawing on a theory-driven narrative literature review, this paper applies an organizational decoupling perspective to distinguish policy–practice decoupling, in which established review requirements are not implemented, from means–ends decoupling, in which review takes place but does not effectively serve disclosure quality. Building on research on human oversight and greenwashing, the paper examines the organizational processes underlying these two forms of failure. It develops a conceptual model linking evidence traceability, accountability relationships that enable questioning, and the integration of management controls. The theoretical analysis suggests that access to information, the authority to raise questions, and action in response are interdependent. Communications-oriented incentives may influence reviewers’ attention to different kinds of evidence, while feedback across reporting cycles influences whether corrections support organizational learning. Three propositions are developed, together with alternative explanations and boundary conditions. The theoretical contribution is to explain why human involvement can produce different outcomes and to distinguish procedural completion, disclosure quality, and sustainability performance. No new experimental or survey data were collected. The proposed relationships remain to be empirically tested.

latest.title: People know who to ask for favors despite underestimating compliance
latest.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
latest.abstract: Whether and how people approach social interactions hinges on how they expect others to respond. Extensive social psychology research suggests that people are inaccurate interpersonal perceivers, overestimating negative responses (e.g., discomfort) and underestimating positive responses (e.g., appreciation) across a variety of social situations. However, this conclusion is based almost exclusively on mean-level bias analyses that obscure the dyadic nature of interpersonal judgment and rely on a narrow conceptualization of interpersonal accuracy. Leveraging research on favor-asking and anticipated compliance as an exemplar, we demonstrate that interpersonal accuracy takes multiple theoretically distinct forms, and that the prevailing conclusion that people misunderstand their influence over others—because they tend to underestimate compliance—is likely overgeneralized. Across four studies (13,196 directed dyadic ratings), we show that people accurately differentiate between who will comply with their favor requests (dyadic meta-accuracy) despite the average tendency to underestimate compliance (mean-level bias). This pattern emerged for specific and general favor requests, among well- and newly-acquainted individuals, and beyond what could be expected due to self-projection. Through this dyadic lens, people are highly adept judges of their influence over others, as they are able to target their requests toward individuals who are uniquely likely to acquiesce to them—and can avoid wasting time on those who are not. Thus, our research refines existing implications for how people approach asking for favors. More broadly, by aligning theory, measurement, and level of analysis, our studies elucidate the need for greater theoretical precision and empirical breadth in interpers

latest.title: Public discourse on violence in medical settings and its implications for medical students' career resilience: evidence from social media text mining
latest.abstract: Background Violence in medical settings has become a growing concern, yet the potential relevance of this public discourse to the career-development environment surrounding medical students remains underexplored. This study investigates the external discursive environment surrounding medical violence and its potential implications for medical students' professional identity and resilience. Methods This study used computational text analysis of public comments on Sina Weibo about violence in medical settings. Guided LDA was applied to 13,101 comments containing at least one retained vocabulary term, while sentiment analysis was conducted on 14,115 comments with usable token sequences. Career Adaptability and Psychological Capital theories informed seed-word selection and the interpretation of the findings. Results Three primary topics emerged: occupational safety (32.9%), professional ethics (30.3%), and professional identification (36.8%) under dominant-topic assignment. Positive sentiment accounted for 63.9% of comments, negative sentiment for 33.1%, and neutral sentiment for 3.0%. Conclusions Positive sentiment predominated, but substantial negative sentiment remained. These patterns characterize a heterogeneous external discursive environment potentially relevant to medical students' career resilience, without establishing individual effects.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Algorithmic Advantage: How Artificial Intelligence (AI) Shapes Audit Firms Performance in Ghana
latest.venue: Journal of risk and financial management
latest.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming auditing process and methodology by shifting the profession from retrospective sampling to continuous, population-wide assurance and predictive risk management. But little is known about how this technology affects audit firms’ overall performance in emerging economies. This research aims to address these issues by exploring the impact of AI adoption in auditing on performance and the extent to which organizational agility mediates this influence, while organizational culture and learning moderate it. The study collected responses from 226 audit professionals at Big Four audit firms in Ghana through surveys and computer-assisted web interviews using a purposive sampling strategy. The data was analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) 4.11.8 in SmartPLS. The findings indicate that AI adoption improves organizational performance and agility. Organizational agility had a positive and significant impact on organizational performance and partially mediated the relationship between AI adoption and organizational performance. Organizational culture had a significant positive moderating impact on the relationship between AI adoption and organizational performance and between AI adoption and organizational agility. Organizational learning significantly and positively moderates the relationship between organizational agility and organizational performance. This study underscores the need for organisations to align strategic AI investments with organizational capabilities to maximize organizational performance in emerging economies.

latest.title: A fragmented ecosystem: ephemerality and standardization gaps in digital serious games designed to counter misinformation
latest.abstract: Introduction The proliferation of online misinformation has prompted the development of a growing number of digital serious games designed to strengthen users' competencies in identifying and resisting false or misleading content. However, comparing their design, theoretical foundations, and evaluation evidence requires attention to how interventions are described and documented. Methods This study combines a scoping review with a framework-based qualitative comparative analysis of six digital serious games represented in seven eligible peer-reviewed publications. The framework examined core design features, pedagogical and theoretical foundations, communicative mechanisms, and motivational design using the eight Core Drives of Octalysis. Results Within this corpus, the analysis identified variation in interaction mechanics, player roles, instructional strategies, motivational features, and evaluation approaches. Variation was not treated as fragmentation in itself; fragmentation concerned barriers to comparison, reproduction, and cumulative development. Four interconnected dimensions were identified: design fragmentation, theoretical fragmentation, evaluation fragmentation, and technological ephemerality. Differences in outcome measures and documentation complicated comparison, while restricted access to some interventions required documentary or archival reconstruction. Discussion These findings provide an exploratory account of the included games and do not establish the prevalence of fragmentation across the wider field. We identify four priority directions for future research: standardized game design taxonomies, longitudinal evaluation protocols, evaluation methods that distinguish discrimination from response bias, and collaborative co-design frameworks.

latest.title: Strategic Agility and Sustainable Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Nakuru County, Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: Strategic agility is the capacity of a firm to sense changes in its operating environment, anticipate alternative futures and reconfigure its resources and operations in good time. It has become a critical capability for manufacturing firms, which operate in an increasingly uncertain environment characterised by economic instability, supply chain disruptions, climate variability and rising production costs. In Nakuru County, Kenya, many manufacturing firms still respond to such disruptions reactively, and evidence on how agility practices relate to their ability to sustain performance remains limited. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the influence of strategic agility on sustainable performance of manufacturing firms in Nakuru County, Kenya. It explored four practices, namely environmental scanning, scenario planning, strategic flexibility and early warning systems. The study was anchored on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Complexity Theory, the Resource-Based View and Organizational Learning Theory. The study adopted a descriptive and explanatory research design and targeted the 34 manufacturing firms in the county. A census of the firms was undertaken and four managers, comprising senior, operations and strategy managers, were purposively selected from each firm, giving 136 respondents, of whom 96 returned completed questionnaires. Structured questionnaires were used to collect data. Both descriptive and inferential statistical methods were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four practices jointly explained 43.9% of the variation in sustainable performance. Environmental scanning was the strongest predictor of sustainable performance, followed by scenario planning and early warning sys

latest.title: Accelerating Sustainability Transitions in Resource‐Constrained and Institutionally Fragile Markets: The Role of ESG Strategies and Sustainable Innovation
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The increasing global emphasis on corporate sustainability has positioned environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance as a critical element of corporate governance and long‐term value creation. However, firms in emerging economies, particularly those within sub‐Saharan Africa (SSA) under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), continue to face challenges in advancing ESG practices due to institutional weaknesses, governance complexities, and financing constraints. This study examines the impact of corporate ownership structure on ESG performance among 497 manufacturing firms in SSA BRI economies from 2013 to 2023. It further investigates the mediating role of innovation capacity, represented by technological innovation and environmental innovation, and the moderating role of financing decisions, measured by equity and debt financing. Grounded in the resource‐based view, stakeholder theory, and institutional theory, the study employs dynamic generalized method of moments (GMM) estimation to address endogeneity concerns and applies MMQR to capture heterogeneous effects. The findings reveal that management, state, family, and foreign ownership positively influence ESG performance, whereas institutional and blockholder ownership negatively affect ESG outcomes. Technological and environmental innovation significantly mediate the ownership–ESG relationship. Furthermore, equity financing strengthens this relationship, whereas debt financing weakens it. The study also identifies significant heterogeneity across regional, policy, and industry contexts. The study contributes to corporate sustainability literature by integrating ownership structures, innovation capacity, and financing decisions into the ESG framework. The findings provide practical insights for po

latest.title: Robots as lab partners: chemists’ perspectives for informing the design of robot-assisted experimentation
latest.abstract: Experimental laboratory work involves repetitive, labour-intensive manual procedures and strict safety protocols, making it an attractive area for Robotics and Artificial Intelligence (RAI). With research currently focused on technical innovation, there has been little work investigating the human factors of chemist-robot collaboration, and how these technologies will change the nature of work in chemistry. Understanding chemists’ requirements and perspectives is vital to the successful deployment and acceptance of RAI in laboratories. We examined the potential for robot-assisted chemistry experimentation through the perspective of future users by conducting contextual inquiries and semi-structured interviews with nine experimental chemists at various career levels with and without laboratory automation experience. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to gain a situated understanding of how their work could benefit from automation, as well as their perspectives and opinions on working alongside robots. We found that our participants are open to robot-assisted experimentation and have clear ideas for human-robot partnerships in the lab. We identified eight themes characterising chemists’ desired applications, the implementation requirements, and the perspectives on the adoption of robot-assisted experimentation. These findings show that successful acceptance of robot-assisted experimentation depends not only on technical innovation, but also on addressing the practical barriers and concerns of the chemists who will work alongside these systems. The key concern being that RAI should not constrain, but rather complement the role of the chemist in knowledge discovery. The findings contribute to a set of initial design considerations covering hardware, software, and interact

latest.title: ENDORSEMENT STRATEGIES AND CONSUMER PERCEPTIONS OF THE HALAL B ERL COSMETIC BRAND (A CASE STUDY OF TIKTOK USERS)
latest.venue: Count Journal of Accounting Business and Management
latest.abstract: TikTok's growth has shifted consumers from chasing viral trends toward seeking authenticity before purchasing, even as trust in influencer-driven endorsement culture continues to decline. This shift is evident in B Erl Cosmetics, a halal cosmetics brand whose policy of refusing collaboration with endorsers seen as contradicting its religious values went viral on TikTok in February 2026. This study aims to examine how B Erl Cosmetics' endorsement strategy on TikTok is perceived as authentic by Generation Z consumers and how this perception shapes brand trust and the brand's halal image. The study employs a qualitative case study approach through semi-structured in-depth interviews with five purposively selected Generation Z informants, analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis grounded in Brand Authenticity Theory. The findings show that all informants perceived B Erl Cosmetics' endorser selection policy as a genuine commitment to protecting its halal brand image rather than mere image- building, although the basis of this perceived sincerity varied, ranging from the owner's personal struggle narrative to reputational-risk reasoning and intuitive belief, while most informants also reported increased brand trust and positive purchase intention. The study concludes that the religiously grounded endorsement policy is perceived as authentic by consumers, thereby strengthening brand trust and the halal brand image of B Erl Cosmetics among Generation Z TikTok users.

latest.title: PENGARUH INTERAKSI LIVE STREAMING, FoMO, DAN BEAUTY INFLUENCER TERHADAP SPONTANEOUS BUYING
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh interaksi live streaming, fear of missing out (FoMO), dan beauty influencer terhadap spontaneous buying beauty brand di TikTok Shop. Fenomena meningkatnya dominasi kategori beauty and care pada platform tersebut menunjukkan adanya pergeseran perilaku konsumen yang dipengaruhi oleh stimulus digital dan faktor psikologis. Perkembangan fitur interaktif seperti siaran langsung, promosi terbatas, serta rekomendasi dari influencer turut menciptakan pengalaman belanja yang lebih persuasif dan emosional. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei terhadap konsumen Generasi Z di Sidoarjo yang pernah melakukan pembelian produk beauty melalui TikTok Shop. Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan purposive sampling dengan jumlah responden sebanyak 98 orang. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan regresi linear berganda untuk menguji pengaruh masing-masing variabel independen terhadap spontaneous buying. Hasil penelitian diharapkan mampu memberikan bukti empiris mengenai peran interaksi real-time dalam live streaming, dorongan psikologis FoMO, serta kredibilitas beauty influencer dalam memengaruhi keputusan pembelian tidak terencana. Selain itu, penelitian ini juga bertujuan untuk mengidentifikasi variabel yang paling dominan memengaruhi perilaku pembelian spontan. Temuan ini diharapkan dapat memperkaya kajian perilaku konsumen dalam konteks social commerce serta menjadi referensi strategis bagi pelaku bisnis dalam merancang pemasaran digital yang efektif dan berorientasi pada pengalaman konsumen.

latest.title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance Terhadap Kinerja Keuangan Perusahaan the Influence of Good Corporate Governance On Company Financial Performance
latest.venue: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
latest.abstract: Good Corporate Governance (GCG) merupakan seperangkat peraturan dan prinsip yang diterapkan untuk meningkatkan sistem serta proses pengelolaan organisasi melalui pengaturan dan penegasan hubungan, kewenangan, hak, serta kewajiban seluruh pemangku kepentingan, termasuk Rapat Umum Pemegang Saham (RUPS), Direksi, dan Dewan Komisaris. Penerapan Good Corporate Governance menjadi salah satu aspek penting dalam menciptakan tata kelola perusahaan yang efektif, transparan, akuntabel, dan bertanggung jawab. Tata kelola perusahaan yang baik diharapkan mampu meningkatkan kepercayaan pemangku kepentingan serta mendukung pencapaian kinerja keuangan perusahaan secara optimal. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Good Corporate Governance terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan memanfaatkan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan keuangan dan laporan tahunan perusahaan. Teknik pengambilan sampel yang digunakan adalah purposive sampling, yaitu pemilihan sampel berdasarkan kriteria tertentu yang telah ditetapkan sesuai dengan kebutuhan penelitian. Metode analisis data yang digunakan adalah regresi data panel dengan bantuan perangkat lunak EViews versi 9. Analisis dilakukan untuk mengetahui hubungan serta pengaruh variabel Good Corporate Governance terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Good Corporate Governance berpengaruh positif terhadap kinerja keuangan perusahaan. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa penerapan tata kelola perusahaan yang baik dapat mendukung peningkatan kinerja keuangan melalui pengelolaan organisasi yang lebih efektif, peningkatan transparansi, serta pengawasan yang optimal terhadap aktivitas perusahaan. latest.title: Lived trajectories of wellbeing in a Triguna-based Sattvik practice ecology
latest.abstract: Subjective wellbeing research has been criticized for theoretical fragmentation, weak causal modeling, and limited cultural grounding, prompting calls for culturally grounded process models of flourishing. This study examines how far the constructs of the Integrated Triguna Framework (ITF), a process model of wellbeing derived from Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS), are recognizable in, qualified by, or exceeded by the retrospective accounts of practitioners engaged with a Sattvik practice ecology in a single bhakti (devotional) community. Fourteen adults (nine male, five female; aged 18–60) were interviewed with a theory-anchored semi-structured guide. Thirteen narrated their own trajectories of practice, which ranged from under 2 years to more than two decades; one long-term practitioner who is also a mental-health professional served as a key informant. Transcripts were analyzed with Template Analysis in a hybrid deductive–inductive stance, supported by an audit trail, explicit disconfirmation criteria, and a negative-case search. Seven themes describe a reported movement from Rajas – Tamas dysregulation, through externally scaffolded entry and embodied discipline, to imperfect, effortful stabilization. Most core ITF constructs were recognizable in the accounts, and Agent– Kṣetra co-evolution was the most extensively described. Some constructs needed refinement. Reported persistence differed according to whether supports were maintained or disrupted, so each persistence-related construct was divided into two variants. Entry into practice followed three routes: through family, through the devotional community, and through media. One participant's entry through social-media content suggested a provisional Digital Kṣetra construct. Negative cases indicate that, in this com

latest.title: The impact of AI-enabled green marketing on consumers’ willingness to pay in transition economy: the role of green perceived quality
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on signaling theory and cue utilization theory, this study aims to examine the relationships among AI-GM, green brand image (GBI), green trust (GT) and willingness to pay (WTP), while also testing the moderating role of green perceived quality (GPQ). Design/methodology/approach This study used PLS-SEM to analyze data from 856 sustainable coffee consumers in Vietnam. Findings The findings indicate that AI-GM positively influences both GBI and GT, and that AI-GM, GBI and GT significantly affect WTP. Furthermore, GBI is positively associated with GT, and GPQ exerts a moderating effect on the relationship between AI-GM and GT. Practical implications The findings confirmed that simultaneously leveraging signaling theory and cue utilization theory are pivotal to study how firms should prioritize clear and credible communication of their green products and initiatives. Moreover, emphasizing trust and long-term commitment to sustainability is essential for stimulating WTP. Such theories are relevant and important not only in developed economies but also in transition economies. Originality/value By leveraging signaling theory and cue utilization theory, this study developed a theoretical model about the moderating effects of green perceived quality (GPQ) on the relationship among AI-GM, green brand image (GBI), green trust (GT) and WTP in a transition economy. This study extends the green marketing literature in the context of AI and provides practical implications for sustainable coffee business in Vietnam.

latest.title: Mental resilience, fear of COVID-19, and psychological distress: a cross-sectional study among chronic disease patients in a regional Greek catchment
latest.venue: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology
latest.abstract: Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted global mental health, with fear of the virus emerging as a key factor statistically linked to psychological distress. While several studies have explored these effects in the general population, chronic disease patients represent a particularly vulnerable subgroup. This study aimed to investigate the associations between fear of COVID-19, mental resilience, and psychological distress (depression, anxiety, and stress) among chronic disease patients in a regional Greek hospital serving a mixed semi-urban and rural catchment. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 293 chronic disease patients at the General Hospital of Argolida, Greece. Participants were recruited using systematic random sampling. An initial missing-data screen included Little’s MCAR test; final regression models used model-wise complete cases. Fear of COVID-19 and psychological distress were assessed using the Fear of COVID-19 Scale (FCV-19S) and the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21), respectively. Resilience was assessed using the 20 CD-RISC items available in the archived participant-level dataset (items 1–20 of the parent CD-RISC-25). The resilience score was calculated as 1.25 x the sum of the 20 items and was available for participants with valid responses to all 20 items (n = 255); no item-level imputation was performed. The final regression models used model-wise complete cases (n = 233 for depression, n =243 for anxiety, and n = 238 for stress). latest.title: The Future: Predicted or Created?
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This article examines the prediction made in 1960 concerning November 13, 2026, and explores its broader implications through mathematics, science, psychology, media, religion, technology, environmental challenges, and humanity's responsibility for the future. Using an analytical and question-based approach, the article considers the relationship between prediction, uncertainty, fear, knowledge, and human choices. It also raises questions about how scientific developments and social beliefs influence the way people understand and shape the future. The article is based on the author's personal studies, reasoning, and perspectives. It is intended to encourage reflection, discussion, and further exploration of the subjects addressed.

hot.title: Trust in scientists and their role in society across 68 countries
hot.abstract: Science is crucial for evidence-based decision-making. Public trust in scientists can help decision makers act on the basis of the best available evidence, especially during crises. However, in recent years the epistemic authority of science has been challenged, causing concerns about low public trust in scientists. We interrogated these concerns with a preregistered 68-country survey of 71,922 respondents and found that in most countries, most people trust scientists and agree that scientists should engage more in society and policymaking. We found variations between and within countries, which we explain with individual- and country-level variables, including political orientation. While there is no widespread lack of trust in scientists, we cannot discount the concern that lack of trust in scientists by even a small minority may affect considerations of scientific evidence in policymaking. These findings have implications for scientists and policymakers seeking to maintain and increase trust in scientists.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Job demands-resources and conservation of resources theories: How do they help to explain employee well-being and future job design?
hot.abstract: This paper examines the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory to understand and predict employee well-being and performance. COR theory suggests that individuals aim to acquire, protect, and maximize resources to reduce psychological distress and prevent burnout. JD-R theory posits that balancing job demands and resources affects employee well-being, behaviors, and performance. By exploring these theories together, the paper offers insights into supporting the workforce amid challenges like remote work and technological advancements. It highlights shared features and differences between the theories, unresolved issues, and research opportunities, such as operationalizing and testing COR theory and differentiating job demands and resources in JD-R theory. The paper concludes with predictions about future job design, emphasizing the need to balance job demands and resources to support employee well-being and performance, contributing to the literature by challenging and refining these theories.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.
