Wang acknowledges financial support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grant 72072004]. Y. Bai acknowledges financial support from the National Social Science Fu

latest.title: A qualitative assessment of perceived resilience in agricultural marketing cooperatives
latest.venue: Journal of Co-operative Organization and Management
latest.abstract: Agricultural marketing cooperatives are vital to agricultural systems, yet their resilience remains understudied. This research applies and extends the resilience assessment framework for farm systems to these cooperatives, examining robustness, adaptability, transformability, and anticipation. Using a qualitative approach, we conducted in-depth interviews with 18 German cooperative decision-makers from December 2023 to February 2024 to examine their perceptions of resilience. Our study employs thematic analysis and deductive category formation to investigate the framework's applicability, gain insights into perceived resilience capacities and strategies, and examine how cooperative values are perceived to foster resilience through the resilience capacities. Results show the adapted framework effectively captures unique cooperative aspects from the perspective of interviewees. Respondents generally describe their organizations as robust and diversified, and as maintaining resilience through adaptability in business fields and functions. While overall resilience is perceived as high, individual capacities vary, with robustness rated highest and anticipatory capacity lowest. Cooperative values are viewed by respondents as contributing to resilience, especially during crises, but are also described as facing challenges. This study provides one of the first systematic qualitative analyses of perceived resilience in agricultural marketing cooperatives and contributes to understanding factors that may support stability and sustainability in food systems.

latest.title: Extending reach while maintaining oversight: Clinicians' perspectives on digital mental health implementation in youth services
latest.abstract: Background Digital mental health interventions (DMHIs) offer a promising means of extending care for children and adolescents, yet their integration into routine clinical services remains inconsistent. The implementation conditions clinicians identify as prerequisites for adoption carry greater relevance given the emergence of AI tools now being used by young people. This study examined the perspectives of mental health professionals (MHPs) working with children and young people to identify key implementation considerations for the development and adoption of DMHIs. Methods Nineteen focus groups were conducted with 50 mental health clinicians from a range of service settings in Queensland, Australia between May 2020 and May 2021. Data were analyzed using a mixed deductive-inductive thematic approach informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Results MHPs were cautiously optimistic about DMHIs, viewing them as most valuable when implemented as supplementary rather than replacement tools. Key perceived uses included waitlist support, screening and assessment, between-session engagement, and flexible treatment pathways. However, MHPs consistently emphasized the need to preserve clinical judgement and oversight across all stages of DMHI use. Risk management, duty of care, and privacy and confidentiality were identified as critical prerequisites for implementation. Conclusions Successful DMHI implementation in child and adolescent mental health services requires flexible, clinician-centered integration approaches, robust risk management protocols, and clear organizational frameworks delineating clinician responsibility. As AI tools are adopted by young people largely outside clinical oversight, these findings offer a grounded baseline for eval
keywords: child and adolescent mental health services

latest.title: A Study of Convergence and Consolidation in Telecom, Media & Entertainment, and E-Commerce Industry in India and Its Business Implications
latest.abstract: In recent years, India has emerged as one of the fastest-growing digital economies globally, with the largest and most active online user bases in the world. This wind of the current digital revolution led by 3G/4G/5G networks is leading to the emergence of the digital convergence phenomenon. In the relentless evolution of technology and markets, many industries are going through major configurations and structural changes where convergence is taking place at the nexus of the telecom, media & entertainment, and e-commerce industries, which has now emerged to become a complete separate industry, the 'TME' industry. So, as these unrelated industries are converging, this study is aimed at understanding the long-term implications of this confluence, so that timely strategic pathways can be adopted by the leaders of these companies. The study's results are based on the analysis of data collected from a sample of 497 consumers from the Delhi-NCR Region of India. The data were collected through a carefully designed, structured questionnaire administered via survey. The empirical analysis was performed by testing the hypothesis using the Mean, Standard deviation, and ANOVA test. The key takeaways emerging from this analysis are expected to provide meaningful value to the leaders and managers of the TME industry. It is found that the dominance of telecom companies in the M&E and e-commerce industry has shuffled the entire industry dynamics by directly competing with global giants like Netflix, Disney, Amazon, Walmart's Flipkart.

latest.title: AN ANALYSIS OF FACTORS INFLUENCING SUSTAINABLE CONSUMPTION BEHAVIORS AMONG GENERATION Z IN KAZAKHSTAN
latest.abstract: This study explores the attitudes and behaviors of Generation Z in Kazakhstan toward sustainable consumption and considers implications for marketers seeking to engage this environmentally conscious demographic. Drawing on a survey of 329 university students, the research examines factors influencing Gen Z’s sustainable behaviors, including environmental concern, social influence, and perceptions of sustainable product pricing. The results reveal a significant positive correlation between environmental concern and engagement in sustainable practices, indicating that Gen Z shows a preference for eco-friendly products and brands committed to sustainability. Given the higher prices of eco-friendly options, pricing remains an important consideration in Gen Z’s sustainable purchasing decisions. Findings emphasize the importance of transparent communication and authentic sustainability practices in building trust and loyalty with this demographic. Marketers should align their strategies with Gen Z’s values by adopting pricing approaches that support eco-friendly choices and leveraging social media to foster communities of conscious consumers.

latest.title: KAZLEATHER 2030: A POLICY FRAMEWORK FOR TRANSFORMING KAZAKHSTAN’S LEATHER INDUSTRY
latest.abstract: The article considers the development of the leather industry of Kazakhstan in the context of industry diversification and sustainable production. The goal of the research is to assess the current state of the leather industry and develop policyoriented recommendations to transform it into a competitive and environmentally sustainable industry. The methodology uses a mixed-methods approach that includes analysis of official statistical data, policy analysis, and semi-structured interviews with key industry actors. The findings indicate that the industry is characterized by limited deep processing, underutilized capacity, environmental costs, weak institutional coordination, and a shortage of personnel. Based on the comparative analysis of the European Union, Türkiye, China, and Uzbekistan, a framework concept for the KazLeather 2030 transformation is proposed that includes the e-vet&Traceability digital platform, the KazLeather Research Grant and the implementation of the KazLeather environmental standard. The research contributes to discussions on modernizing resource-based industries and offers practical instruments for upgrading value-added chains.

latest.title: Pengaruh Perilaku Konsumtif Pengguna Shopee terhadap Manajemen Keuangan Generasi Z di Pariaman Tengah
latest.abstract: The ease of conducting transactions through e-commerce, particularly Shopee, may encourage consumptive behavior that can affect Generation Z’s financial management. This study aimed to analyze the effect of consumptive behavior among Shopee users on the financial management of Generation Z in Pariaman Tengah Subdistrict. The study used a quantitative approach with a survey method involving 100 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using simple linear regression, a t-test, and the coefficient of determination. The results showed that consumptive behavior had a negative and significant regression coefficient for financial management (t = −5.190; p < 0.001), with the regression equation Y = 40.553 − 0.184X. The coefficient of determination (R² = 0.216) indicated that the model explained 21.6% of the variation in financial management, while the remaining 78.4% of the variation was not explained by the model. These findings indicate that the higher the level of consumptive behavior, the lower the respondents’ financial management ability. This study provides empirical evidence of the relationship between consumptive behavior and financial management among Generation Z in Pariaman Tengah Subdistrict and emphasizes the importance of controlling consumptive behavior and practicing prudent financial management when conducting transactions through Shopee.

latest.title: Pengaruh Mikrotransaksi Game Online terhadap Pengelolaan Keuangan Mahasiswa (Survei pada Mahasiswa Jurusan Akuntansi Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Universitas Halu Oleo)
latest.venue: Jurnal Semesta Ilmu Manajemen dan Ekonomi
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh mikrotransaksi game online terhadap pengelolaan keuangan mahasiswa Jurusan Akuntansi Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Universitas Halu Oleo. Populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah mahasiswa Jurusan Akuntansi Fakultas Ekonomi dan Bisnis Universitas Halu Oleo angkatan 2022–2025. Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan metode purposive sampling, sehingga diperoleh 90 responden. Jenis data yang digunakan adalah data kuantitatif dengan sumber data primer yang diperoleh melalui penyebaran kuesioner. Metode analisis data menggunakan regresi linear sederhana dengan bantuan software IBM SPSS versi 31. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa mikrotransaksi game online berpengaruh negatif terhadap pengelolaan keuangan mahasiswa. Hal ini menunjukkan bahwa semakin tinggi intensitas mahasiswa dalam melakukan mikrotransaksi, maka kemampuan mereka dalam mengelola keuangan cenderung menurun. Berdasarkan hasil penelitian dapat disimpulkan bahwa mikrotransaksi memiliki pengaruh negatif terhadap pengelolaan keuangan mahasiswa, sehingga mahasiswa disarankan untuk mampu meningkatkan pengendalian keuangan, khususnya dalam pengeluaran pada mikrotransaksi game online.

latest.title: THE IMPACT OF LABOR DISPATCH EMPLOYMENT ON BANK PERFORMANCE: INSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS, MECHANISMS, AND AN EMPIRICAL IDENTIFICATION FRAMEWORK
latest.abstract: Labor dispatch employment is a staffing form widely discussed in the banking sector under pressure from branch transformation, cost control, and flexible service provision, but its impact on bank performance is not unidirectional. Based on human capital architecture theory, transaction cost theory, organizational flexibility theory, psychological contract theory, and operational risk theory, and integrating the characteristics of the banking industry—knowledge intensity, reputation sensitivity, strong regulation, and risk contagion—this paper constructs a fourfold mechanism of "cost flexibility—service efficiency—risk compliance—human capital stability." This paper proposes that the relationship between the proportion of labor dispatch employment and banks' risk-adjusted performance may follow an inverted U-shape: moderate use can reduce rigid employment costs and enhance numerical flexibility and efficiency in auxiliary positions, whereas excessive use harms performance through coordination and supervision costs, compliance costs, operational risk, and declining service quality; job criticality, regulatory intensity, equal pay for equal work enforcement, and digitalization level constitute important moderating variables. In terms of research design, this paper recommends bank-year panel fixed effects models, instrumental variable methods, propensity score matching, and a difference-in-differences identification strategy using the Interim Provisions on Labor Dispatch as a shock, with employee stability, service continuity, operational risk, and compliance costs as mediating channels. This paper does not report fabricated data or empirical results, but instead provides testable propositions, a variable system, and a causal identification framework, offering a theoretical

latest.title: Analysis of HR Administration Implementation in Workload Management and Work Communication in the Rooms Department Division of Anara Sky Kualanamu Hotel
latest.venue: International Journal of Management Research and Economics
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the implementation of Human Resources (HR) administration regarding workload management and workplace communication within the Rooms Division of Anara Sky Kualanamu Hotel. The study is contextualized by the dynamic operational nature of the hotel industry-specifically within the Rooms Division, which faces fluctuating workloads due to changes in occupancy rates, guest service requirements, and work schedules. Furthermore, effective workplace communication is crucial for supporting staff coordination and operational smoothness. Poorly managed workloads and ineffective communication can lead to misunderstandings, hinder coordination, and potentially impact service quality. This study employs a qualitative method with a descriptive approach. Informants were selected using purposive sampling, involving individuals with direct knowledge and experience regarding HR administration, workload management, and workplace communication within the Rooms Division. Data collection was conducted through interviews, observation, and documentation. A qualitative approach was utilized to gain an in-depth understanding of HR administration practices, as well as the informants' experiences and perceptions regarding actual working conditions.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Public discourse on violence in medical settings and its implications for medical students' career resilience: evidence from social media text mining
latest.abstract: Background Violence in medical settings has become a growing concern, yet the potential relevance of this public discourse to the career-development environment surrounding medical students remains underexplored. This study investigates the external discursive environment surrounding medical violence and its potential implications for medical students' professional identity and resilience. Methods This study used computational text analysis of public comments on Sina Weibo about violence in medical settings. Guided LDA was applied to 13,101 comments containing at least one retained vocabulary term, while sentiment analysis was conducted on 14,115 comments with usable token sequences. Career Adaptability and Psychological Capital theories informed seed-word selection and the interpretation of the findings. Results Three primary topics emerged: occupational safety (32.9%), professional ethics (30.3%), and professional identification (36.8%) under dominant-topic assignment. Positive sentiment accounted for 63.9% of comments, negative sentiment for 33.1%, and neutral sentiment for 3.0%. Conclusions Positive sentiment predominated, but substantial negative sentiment remained. These patterns characterize a heterogeneous external discursive environment potentially relevant to medical students' career resilience, without establishing individual effects.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Pengaruh Kinerja Keuangan, Inventory Intensity, dan Financial Distress terhadap Tax Avoidance pada Sektor Consumer Non-Cyclicals
latest.venue: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
latest.abstract: Praktik penghindaran pajak (tax avoidance) masih menjadi persoalan serius dalam upaya optimalisasi penerimaan negara, sementara hasil penelitian terdahulu mengenai faktor-faktor yang memengaruhinya masih belum konsisten. Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji dan menganalisis pengaruh kinerja keuangan, inventory intensity, dan financial distress terhadap tax avoidance pada perusahaan sektor Consumer Non-Cyclicals yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020–2024. Penelitian ini merupakan penelitian asosiatif dengan metode kuantitatif yang menggunakan data sekunder berupa laporan keuangan dan laporan tahunan perusahaan. Dari populasi sebanyak 128 perusahaan, sampel dipilih dengan teknik purposive sampling sehingga diperoleh 36 perusahaan dengan 180 data observasi. Kinerja keuangan diproksikan dengan Return on Assets, inventory intensity dengan rasio total persediaan terhadap total aset, financial distress dengan Altman Z-Score, dan tax avoidance dengan Effective Tax Rate. Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi data panel dengan bantuan EViews 14. Berdasarkan uji Chow, uji Hausman, dan uji Lagrange Multiplier, model yang terpilih adalah Random Effect Model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kinerja keuangan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap tax avoidance, sedangkan inventory intensity dan financial distress tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap tax avoidance. Secara simultan, kinerja keuangan, inventory intensity, dan financial distress berpengaruh signifikan terhadap tax avoidance, dengan kemampuan menjelaskan sebesar 3,70%. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa perusahaan dengan kinerja keuangan yang semakin baik cenderung memiliki Effective Tax Rate yang lebih rendah, sehingga tingkat tax avoidance yang dilakukan lebih tinggi.

latest.title: Strategic Agility and Sustainable Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Nakuru County, Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: Strategic agility is the capacity of a firm to sense changes in its operating environment, anticipate alternative futures and reconfigure its resources and operations in good time. It has become a critical capability for manufacturing firms, which operate in an increasingly uncertain environment characterised by economic instability, supply chain disruptions, climate variability and rising production costs. In Nakuru County, Kenya, many manufacturing firms still respond to such disruptions reactively, and evidence on how agility practices relate to their ability to sustain performance remains limited. Therefore, the purpose of this study was to examine the influence of strategic agility on sustainable performance of manufacturing firms in Nakuru County, Kenya. It explored four practices, namely environmental scanning, scenario planning, strategic flexibility and early warning systems. The study was anchored on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Complexity Theory, the Resource-Based View and Organizational Learning Theory. The study adopted a descriptive and explanatory research design and targeted the 34 manufacturing firms in the county. A census of the firms was undertaken and four managers, comprising senior, operations and strategy managers, were purposively selected from each firm, giving 136 respondents, of whom 96 returned completed questionnaires. Structured questionnaires were used to collect data. Both descriptive and inferential statistical methods were used to analyse the data, which were presented in tables and discussed. The findings revealed that the four practices jointly explained 43.9% of the variation in sustainable performance. Environmental scanning was the strongest predictor of sustainable performance, followed by scenario planning and early warning sys

latest.title: ENDORSEMENT STRATEGIES AND CONSUMER PERCEPTIONS OF THE HALAL B ERL COSMETIC BRAND (A CASE STUDY OF TIKTOK USERS)
latest.venue: Count Journal of Accounting Business and Management
latest.abstract: TikTok's growth has shifted consumers from chasing viral trends toward seeking authenticity before purchasing, even as trust in influencer-driven endorsement culture continues to decline. This shift is evident in B Erl Cosmetics, a halal cosmetics brand whose policy of refusing collaboration with endorsers seen as contradicting its religious values went viral on TikTok in February 2026. This study aims to examine how B Erl Cosmetics' endorsement strategy on TikTok is perceived as authentic by Generation Z consumers and how this perception shapes brand trust and the brand's halal image. The study employs a qualitative case study approach through semi-structured in-depth interviews with five purposively selected Generation Z informants, analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis grounded in Brand Authenticity Theory. The findings show that all informants perceived B Erl Cosmetics' endorser selection policy as a genuine commitment to protecting its halal brand image rather than mere image- building, although the basis of this perceived sincerity varied, ranging from the owner's personal struggle narrative to reputational-risk reasoning and intuitive belief, while most informants also reported increased brand trust and positive purchase intention. The study concludes that the religiously grounded endorsement policy is perceived as authentic by consumers, thereby strengthening brand trust and the halal brand image of B Erl Cosmetics among Generation Z TikTok users.

latest.title: The impact of AI-enabled green marketing on consumers’ willingness to pay in transition economy: the role of green perceived quality
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on signaling theory and cue utilization theory, this study aims to examine the relationships among AI-GM, green brand image (GBI), green trust (GT) and willingness to pay (WTP), while also testing the moderating role of green perceived quality (GPQ). Design/methodology/approach This study used PLS-SEM to analyze data from 856 sustainable coffee consumers in Vietnam. Findings The findings indicate that AI-GM positively influences both GBI and GT, and that AI-GM, GBI and GT significantly affect WTP. Furthermore, GBI is positively associated with GT, and GPQ exerts a moderating effect on the relationship between AI-GM and GT. Practical implications The findings confirmed that simultaneously leveraging signaling theory and cue utilization theory are pivotal to study how firms should prioritize clear and credible communication of their green products and initiatives. Moreover, emphasizing trust and long-term commitment to sustainability is essential for stimulating WTP. Such theories are relevant and important not only in developed economies but also in transition economies. Originality/value By leveraging signaling theory and cue utilization theory, this study developed a theoretical model about the moderating effects of green perceived quality (GPQ) on the relationship among AI-GM, green brand image (GBI), green trust (GT) and WTP in a transition economy. This study extends the green marketing literature in the context of AI and provides practical implications for sustainable coffee business in Vietnam.

latest.title: The effects of generative AI cues on consumer flow in E-commerce platforms: findings from experiments
Peran Kompetensi Digital Dalam Mendukung Kinerja Sales Melalui Pemanfaatan Media Sosial: Studi Kasus Industri Sepeda Motor
latest.venue: Journal of Business Economics and Management
latest.abstract: This study examines the role of digital competence in supporting sales performance through social media utilization in the motorcycle industry, focusing on Yamaha JG Gunung Sindur Dealer. A qualitative case study approach was employed to explore how sales personnel use digital platforms in their daily activities. Data were collected through interviews with three informants: a salesperson, a sales supervisor, and a consumer. The findings indicate that social media platforms, particularly WhatsApp, Instagram, and Facebook, are utilized to promote motorcycle products, share information about prices and installment plans, attract potential customers, and maintain communication through follow-up activities. The supervisor also plays a supporting role by monitoring digital promotional activities and providing facilities for content creation. However, several challenges remain, including limited time for content production, difficulties in developing creative ideas, and inconsistent customer responses. This study highlights the importance of digital competence in supporting communication and sales activities through social media.

latest.title: Pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility, Leverage, dan Good Corporate Governance terhadap Pengungkapan Emisi Karbon pada Perusahaan Subsektor Food and Beverage yang Terdaftar di BEI Periode 2020-2024
latest.venue: Journal of Business Social and Technology
latest.abstract: Latar Belakang: Pengungkapan emisi karbon (Carbon Emission Disclosure ) merupakan salah satu bentuk transparansi perusahaan dalam mendukung akuntabilitas lingkungan dan pembangunan berkelanjutan. Tujuan: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), leverage, dan Good Corporate Governance (GCG) terhadap pengungkapan emisi karbon pada perusahaan Consumer Non-Cyclicals subsektor Food and Beverage yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2020-2024. Metode: Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan teknik purposive sampling, menghasilkan 16 perusahaan sampel dan 80 observasi data panel. Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi data panel dengan model Fixed Effect yang dikoreksi melalui White cross-section standard errors, dibantu perangkat lunak EViews 13. Hasil: Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa CSR, leverage, dan GCG secara simultan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap pengungkapan emisi karbon dengan Adjusted R² sebesar 0,837. Secara parsial, CSR berpengaruh positif dan signifikan, leverage berpengaruh negatif dan signifikan, sedangkan GCG yang diproksikan dengan ukuran dewan direksi tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap pengungkapan emisi karbon. Kesimpulan: Temuan ini membuktikan bahwa tanggung jawab sosial dan struktur pendanaan perusahaan merupakan determinan penting transparansi emisi karbon, sedangkan ukuran dewan direksi belum cukup untuk mendorong pengungkapan tersebut.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kompetensi Karyawan Dan Kualitas Pelayanan Terhadap Kepuasan Konsumen Pada UMKM Sambal Leunca Kemangi Pamulang
latest.venue: Journal of Business Economics and Management
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of Employee Competence and Service Quality on Consumer Satisfaction at Sambal Leunca Kemangi Pamulang MSME. A quantitative approach with a survey method was applied. Data were collected through questionnaires from 50 respondents who met the research criteria. Multiple linear regression was used with t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination. The results show that Employee Competence has a positive but insignificant effect on Consumer Satisfaction, with a t-value of 1.178 and a significance value of 0.245. Service Quality has a positive and significant effect, with a t-value of 6.712 and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, Employee Competence and Service Quality significantly affect Consumer Satisfaction, with an F-value of 83.695 and a significance value of 0.000. The coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.781 indicates that the model explains 78.1% of the variation in Consumer Satisfaction, while 21.9% is associated with other factors outside the model. The findings indicate that service quality should receive greater managerial attention in improving consumer satisfaction.

latest.title: A Design of an Effective Banking Application with Customer Churn Prediction and Enhanced Market Equilibrium Based Security Testing Through Machine Learning
latest.venue: The International Journal of Maritime Engineering
latest.abstract: Banking application and compliance with the EU PSD2 directive and the impact of protection motivation theory oninformation security. It identifies a gap in PMT literature and examines factors influencing consumer adoption of Fintech banking amidst ongoing digitalization. To overcome this issue, a new model has developed Customer Churn Prediction and Enhanced Market Equilibrium based Security Testing (CCMEST). This investigation proposes that integrating analytical modeling, market analysis, security validation, hypothesis testing, and machine learning will enhance banking applications through a model that factors in labor, capital, management, and effort using a Cobb-Douglas production function to assess firm value-added and managerial incentives and Cumulative distribution function (CDF). Companies will be evaluated on capital, management talent, and their effectiveness in achieving market equilibrium while assessing compensation and value-added. Security Testing involved 19 tests on banking API operations, focusing on secure communication, authentication, transaction fetching, and unauthorized request rejection. Hypothesis Testing evaluated statistical correlations using t-statistics, p-values, and PLS-SEM, with significant results determined by pre-set thresholds. Machine Learning Models applied UMAP for dimensionality reduction, followed by DBSCAN and K-means clustering, favoring K-means for its superior silhouette coefficient of 0.5225 compared to DBSCAN’s 0.5099. The performance analysis is CCMEST ML Model accuracy, precision, recall, F1-Score, CCMEST Overall Performance, CCMEST Overall Performance.

latest.title: Digital transaction frictions in platform service ecosystems: coordination failures and consumer uncertainty
latest.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to conceptualise Digital Transaction Frictions (DTFs) as recurrent, structurally embedded disruptions in platform-mediated service ecosystems and examines how coordination conditions shape consumer uncertainty, transaction-management effort and digital participation through service ecosystem theory and Transformative Service Research. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with 40 participants, comprising 28 consumers and 12 organisational experts. Data were analysed through an abductive, Gioia-informed approach. Findings The findings identify three analytical elements: two ecosystem-level conditions, temporal drift and fragmented accountability and one consumer-level process, adaptive uncertainty. Together, these elements suggest how recurring instability in distributed service arrangements may shift uncertainty and transaction-management work onto consumers. Practical implications The findings suggest that platform operators and logistics partners could complement firm-level monitoring with shared diagnostics across the transaction pathway. Customer experience managers could also treat recurring friction as a signal of systemic misalignment rather than an isolated complaint. Originality/value The study positions DTFs as a complementary ecosystem-level construct that links coordination conditions with recurrent transaction instability and its implications for consumer uncertainty, vulnerability and participation, while distinguishing ecosystem conditions that define DTFs from the consumer outcomes they may produce.

latest.title: When CSR signals fail: perceived quality as a credibility condition for consumer–brand identification
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how corporate social responsibility (CSR) translates into consumer–based brand equity (CBBE) by identifying the mechanisms and conditions underlying this process. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on signaling theory, data from 172 Mexican consumers exposed to a CSR initiative were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings CSR does not generate consumer value through direct effects. Instead, consumer–brand identification acts as the central mechanism linking CSR to CBBE. Empathic concern positively influences identification, but only when perceived quality is high. Under these conditions, effects extend to trust, purchase intention, recommendation intention and engagement. When perceived quality is low, the mechanism collapses. Socially responsible consumption exhibits weak and unstable effects. Social implications Social initiatives are more likely to mobilize consumer trust, engagement and support when social purpose is accompanied by credible organizational performance. Originality/value This study advances CSR research by proposing a conditionally bounded signaling model in which perceived quality serves as the credibility condition that enables or suppresses CSR value creation.

latest.title: Beyond Rational Choice: A Behavioral Game-Theoretic Frameworkfor Consumer Decision-Making
latest.venue: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
latest.abstract: Since Behavioral Economics explains decisions through bounded rationality and mental shortcuts, it is necessary to incorporate strategic interactions into such analyses. This study develops an integrated framework for analyzing irrational purchasing decisions, which includes elements of Behavioral Economics, non-cooperative Game Theory, econometric analysis, and an integrated model of consumer behavior, the Consumer Irrational Utility Model (CIUM). The study employs a quantitative survey of personal care products consumers in the FMCG market, modeling a consumer and a seller as two players in a 2 × 2 non-cooperative game. The game is analyzed using best-response strategies, followed by the derivation of a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium. The results of the game-theoretic model are then tested using Linear Probability Model (LPM) and Weighted Least Squares (WLS) for estimation purposes. The results of the behavioral determinants, validated in the LPM and WLS estimations, are then incorporated into CIUM, which explains how irrational behavior by a consumer deviates from the utility-maximizing behavior of a rational human being. The study reveals that in the Indian FMCG market, consumers mainly adopt the Relative Decision Paradox strategy, whereas sellers mainly adopt the Strategized Pricing strategy. The study further reveals that the behavioral variables identified in the study have a significant impact on consumers' purchasing decisions. Also, results from the CIUM indicate that the economic utility of a product and the utility influenced by various behavioral factors in strategic interactions in the market jointly determine the overall utility of a product for a consumer.

latest.title: The invisible side of the dish: the ethnic food value chain in the Amazon
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to contribute to the fields of operations management and supply chain management by demonstrating that, in the context of ethnic foods, value chains must move beyond merely symbolic appreciation of territory and incorporate recognition of actors at the base of the chain to promote social justice. Design/methodology/approach Using a qualitative approach, the findings demonstrate that, although fish products hold high symbolic value, structural inequalities persist throughout the value chain. Findings Artisanal fishers remain invisible and their traditional knowledge and demands are neglected in decision-making processes. The concentration of power among intermediaries, combined with the absence of effective institutional support, restricts opportunities and reinforces exclusion. There is also a lack of recognition of these workers’ social identities, a fundamental aspect in promoting a more equitable distribution of the benefits generated. Research limitations/implications This study has limitations related to the specificity of its empirical context and the territorial distances involved, which warrant caution when generalizing the findings. Some fishing villages are located in remote and difficult-to-access areas, which limited the number of participants in the first phase of the research. Practical implications Managers may invest in production verticalization, which could reduce dependence on intermediaries and improve fishers’ remuneration. Chefs can also act as bridges between producers and consumers. Finally, strengthening public policies aimed at ethnic food value chains is essential. Social implications It is essential to promote DEI-oriented public policies and initiatives that value local cultural practices, thereby increasing sustainab

latest.title: Persaingan Harga Dalam Industri E-Commerce di Indonesia Pada Era Live Shopee dan Tokopedia
latest.venue: Journal of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises
latest.abstract: The development of digital technology has increased competition among e-commerce platforms in Indonesia, particularly through live shopping. This competition involves product prices, discounts, vouchers, and free shipping promotions. This study aims to analyze pricing and promotional strategies related to Shopee Live and Tokopedia Play and their implications for business competition and consumer behavior. The research uses a literature review method with a qualitative descriptive approach. Data were collected from relevant scientific articles and analyzed by identifying similarities and differences in their findings. The results indicate that price discounts are commonly associated with increased purchase intention, purchasing decisions, and impulse buying. Live streaming can also influence consumer behavior, although its effects vary across studies. Furthermore, large discounts and shipping subsidies may attract consumers but can put pressure on small business profit margins. Extremely low prices may also raise concerns about unfair business competition under certain conditions. However, the reviewed studies do not provide sufficient direct evidence to determine which platform consistently offers lower prices. Therefore, price competition in live shopping needs to be evaluated by considering promotional strategies, consumer responses, and fair business practices.

latest.title: Innovation constraints in FinTech SMEs: uncovering the structural logic of an emerging digital ecosystem
latest.abstract: Purpose FinTech small and medium enterprises (SMEs) play a growing role in advancing digital financial innovation, yet innovation barriers are often treated as independent factors ranked by importance, obscuring which factors occupy structurally dominant positions relative to others. This study adopts a systems perspective to examine the structural relationships among innovation barriers in FinTech SMEs, using India as an empirical context. Design/methodology/approach The study employs an integrated Modified Delphi-Interpretive Structural Modelling (ISM)-MICMAC framework. A panel of 22 domain specialists participated in barrier validation, while 16 experts participated in the structural modelling phase to analyse 13 validated innovation barriers affecting FinTech SMEs. Findings Regulatory Complexity and Regulatory Uncertainty are structurally inferred to occupy the most dominant position in the innovation constraint system, connecting downstream to compliance costs, financial limitations, and technological and organisational constraints, and ultimately to outcomes such as consumer trust and demand uncertainty. MICMAC analysis identifies a stable two-cluster structure comprising six Independent (Driver) barriers and seven Dependent barriers, demonstrating the hierarchical and systemic nature of innovation constraints within regulated digital ecosystems. Originality/value The study demonstrates that innovation constraints in FinTech SMEs constitute a hierarchically structured system in which institutional and regulatory conditions occupy the most structurally dominant position. By moving beyond factor-based approaches, the study offers a systems perspective on how innovation constraints propagate within emerging digital ecosystems and identifies foundational intervention

latest.title: Typology of personnel risks in consumer cooperation organizations: empirical analysis and adaptive mechanisms
latest.abstract: The article presents the results of an empirical study of personnel risks in consumer cooperation organizations. The relevance of the study is due to the systemic personnel crisis in the cooperative sector, associated with demographic aging of staff, territorial isolation, and a steady decline in the inflow of young people. The empirical base is survey data from 298 employees of 48 cooperative organizations in sixregions of European Russia and Western Siberia (2025).Using cluster analysis, three types of organizations with different risk profiles were identified: demographically aging (32 % of the sample), territorially deficient (28 %), and motivationally disadvantaged (39 %). Logistic regression confirmed that the share of employees over 50 years old, lack of mentoring, and distance from the district center significantly increase the likelihood of high turnover.Structural equation modeling (SEM) showed that mentoring partially mediates the relationship between distance and youth turnover. A typologically differentiated table of adaptive strategies for each risk type has been developed.The practical significance lies in the creation of a diagnostic tool for regional cooperative unions, allowing them to select an adaptive personnel management mechanism based on four indicators (the share of employees over 50 years old, the presence of mentoring, distance from the district center, and motivational satisfaction), which ensures the implementation of the research results in the activities of cooperative organizations without involving external consultants.

latest.title: Sociology of budol consumption in the Philippines: the construction of reflexive complicit consumer
latest.abstract: Budol consumption, a locally recognized consumption phenomenon, has gained prominence in the Philippine online marketplace yet remains sociologically underexplored. Budol consumption commonly refers to consumers being induced into unnecessary and unplanned purchases, often viewed as impulsive buying. Prevailing psychological and technological theories tend to depict such consumers as passive and manipulated, overlooking the reflexive practices apparent in budol consumption. Likewise, existing theories of reflexive consumption do not fully account for how self-awareness is mobilized in this context. Drawing on analysis of budol- related TikTok content, this article advances two arguments. First, I argue that budol consumers are also reflexive consumers who are active and self-aware, challenging dominant portrayals of impulsive consumers as merely reactive and passive. Second, I demonstrate that self-awareness in budol consumption is mobilized in a distinctive manner that existing understanding of reflexive consumption may not fully capture. Rather than enabling resistance or more informed consumer decisions, reflexivity here leads to complicity with problematic consumption practices. Budol consumers recognize algorithmic/technological infrastructures designed to induce them into consumption but knowingly continue to participate. To account for this dynamic, I proposed the concept of reflexive complicity, which may illuminate other modern, platformized consumption practices.

latest.title: Brand resilience under environmental threat: competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern in seafood purchase intentions
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how brand image shapes seafood purchase intentions under environmental threat. Drawing on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) framework, it examines the competing mediating roles of perceived value and environmental concern. Design/methodology/approach Using a systematic sampling approach, this study collected 319 valid questionnaires from coastal consumers in Guangdong Province, China. Structural equation modeling was used to test the dual-mediation model involving perceived value and environmental concern. Findings Brand image positively influences both perceived value and environmental concern. Perceived value enhances purchase intention, while environmental concern suppresses it. Both variables significantly mediate the brand–purchase relationship in opposing directions, with an overall positive indirect effect, suggesting that brand resilience endures despite ecological concerns. Originality/value This study contributes by modeling competing psychological mediators in seafood consumption under environmental threat, an area that has received limited attention in existing literature. It reveals consumer ambivalence during ecological crises: while strong brands retain appeal, environmental risk awareness weakens purchasing confidence. The findings offer actionable insights for seafood marketers on sustaining brand resilience through value communication and transparent sustainability practices.

latest.title: PENGARUH KETERLIBATAN MEDIA SOSIAL TERHADAP MINAT BERKUNJUNG KE LABUAN BAJO : PERSEPSI NILAI DAN CITRA DESTINASI SEBAGAI VARIABEL MEDIASI
latest.abstract: Social media has become a primary source of travel information and inspiration, yet high exposure does not always translate into strong visit intention. This study analyzes the effect of social media engagement on tourists’ visit intention to Labuan Bajo, both directly and through perceived value and destination image as mediating variables. A quantitative approach with descriptive and verificative methods was applied. Primary data were collected through a questionnaire administered to 100 respondents selected by purposive sampling, namely active social media users who had obtained information about Labuan Bajo through social media and had never visited it. The data were analyzed using PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4. The results show that social media engagement has a positive and significant effect on perceived value (β = 0.421), destination image (β = 0.456), and visit intention (β = 0.405). Perceived value (β = 0.347) and destination image (β = 0.380) also have positive and significant effects on visit intention and partially mediate the effect of social media engagement, with indirect effects of 0.146 and 0.173, respectively. The model explains 81.5% of the variance in visit intention (R² = 0.815), although the overall model fit is not yet optimal. This study contributes by mapping two mediation pathways, value and image, that link social media engagement to the visit intention of prospective tourists to a super-priority tourism destination.

latest.title: Building collaboration in FMCG supply chains: a time-based perspective
latest.venue: Supply Chain Management An International Journal
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how supply chain collaboration (SCC) initiatives in logistics develop and are sustained over time. While SCC is widely discussed in the literature, existing research predominantly adopts static perspectives, treating collaboration mechanisms as stable configurations rather than temporally evolving practices. This study addresses this gap by adopting a temporal, process-oriented perspective on SCC development. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative multiple-case research design, analysing 15 collaboration initiatives across nine companies, comprising major food retailers and multinational producers, operating in the Italian Fast-Moving Consumer Goods sector. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, pre-interview questionnaires and company documentation and analysed through within-case and cross-case analysis. Findings The findings show that collaboration mechanisms do not function uniformly across the lifecycle of an initiative: their role and relevance shift as partnerships mature. The cross-case analysis identifies two additional empirical insights: collaborative function autonomy, the degree of operational independence enjoyed by logistics teams in driving collaboration, and the dual role of time, both as an operational resource and as a relational enabler of trust. Building on these insights, the study proposes a time-based framework mapping how mechanisms are introduced, adapted and sustained across four phases: inception, development, execution and evolution. Practical implications The framework provides managers with a phased roadmap for designing and managing collaborative initiatives, supporting more realistic expectations about the pace of collaboration and the investments required at each st

latest.title: Integrating Social Influence Theory and the Theory of Planned Behavior to Explain Green Drinkware Purchase Intention among Jakarta’s Emerging Adults: The Moderating Role of Economic Constraints
latest.abstract: This study investigated how digital social influence shaped green drinkware purchase intentions among emerging adults in Jakarta by integrating Social Influence Theory (SIT) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB). A quantitative survey was conducted among 400 Jakarta residents aged 20–29 who were familiar with green drinkware and had previously used or purchased such products. The collected data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings revealed that social media engagement positively influenced attitudes and subjective norms, with the relationship between social media engagement and subjective norms exhibiting the strongest path coefficient. Both attitudes and subjective norms positively influenced green label awareness, which, in turn, strengthened green brand trust. Green brand trust subsequently had a positive effect on green purchase intention. Although economic constraints exhibited a negative moderating effect, this relationship was not statistically significant. These findings indicated that social media served not merely as an information dissemination channel but also as a normative environment that shaped consumers' perceptions, attitudes, and behavioral intentions. Furthermore, green purchase intention emerged through a multistage process involving social influence, psychological responses, environmental information awareness, and brand trust. The study contributed to the integration of SIT and TPB by demonstrating the interconnected mechanisms underlying environmentally responsible purchasing intentions. From a practical perspective, the findings highlighted the importance of leveraging social proof in marketing communications, providing credible environmental labeling information, strengthening consume

latest.title: Mapping incivility research across financial services and other high-interaction service sectors: a bibliometric analysis of relational and thematic patterns
latest.abstract: Purpose This study traces the evolution of incivility research across financial services and other high-interaction service sectors. It examines how the literature differs in its treatment of the forms, sources, associated outcomes, and thematic configurations of incivility. It also assesses the extent to which research reflects the transition toward digital service environments and identifies priorities for future research. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis was conducted on 1,259 documents indexed in Scopus and Web of Science, covering the period 1977–2025 and representing 517 scientific sources. Performance, citation, co-word, and thematic analyses were used to examine the field's development and compare its relational and thematic patterns across financial services, retail, hospitality, healthcare, and education. The search included incivility and adjacent forms of interpersonal mistreatment (e.g. bullying, verbal abuse) to map their relationships without treating them as conceptually equivalent. Findings The incivility literature has evolved from an early emphasis on internal workplace relationships in healthcare and education toward greater attention to customer-facing interactions in retail, hospitality, and financial services. The sectoral comparison reveals a relational divide in the literature. Retail and hospitality research primarily frames incivility as originating from customers, whereas healthcare and education research places greater emphasis on coworkers, supervisors, and institutional hierarchies. Financial services combine these patterns, with studies addressing customer and coworker incivility alongside workplace ostracism, job insecurity, employee cynicism, and psychological resources. The theoretical frame also varies: the Conserva
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Transparency matters
latest.abstract: This study examines how sponsorship disclosure format and influencer compensation nature shape perceived sponsorship transparency and its effects on source credibility, information credibility, online engagement, and purchase intention among Instagram micro-influencers. Drawing on the Persuasion Knowledge Model, Communication Transparency Theory, Parasocial Interaction Theory, and Source Credibility Theory, the study conceptualizes perceived sponsorship transparency as consumers’ holistic judgment of how openly the commercial relationship is communicated. A between-subjects experiment (420 participants) was analyzed using two-way analysis of variance, regression, and serial mediation. Disclosure format, but not compensation nature, influenced perceived transparency, with platform-integrated disclosures outperforming hashtag-based ones, extending the Persuasion Knowledge Model to platform-governed ecosystems. Transparency sequentially mediated behavioral outcomes through source and information credibility, with source credibility the stronger mediator. Limitations include snowball sampling, a fictitious influencer and brand, and no confirmatory factor analysis.

latest.title: Financial Leverage, Profitability, and Firm Value: Evidence From Primary Consumer Goods Companies Listed on The Indonesia Stock Exchange
latest.venue: Journal of Capital Markets and Banking
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dan menjelaskan pengaruh Financial Leverage dan Profitabilitas terhadap Nilai Perusahaan pada perusahaan sektor Barang Konsumen Primer yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) selama periode 2019–2024. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif. Populasi penelitian terdiri atas 125 perusahaan, dengan teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria yang telah ditentukan, sehingga diperoleh 10 perusahaan sebagai sampel penelitian. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan metode regresi linier berganda, sedangkan pengolahan data dilakukan dengan bantuan program EViews versi 13. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Financial Leverage dan Profitabilitas secara simultan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan yang diproksikan dengan Price to Book Value (PBV). Secara parsial, Financial Leverage yang diproksikan dengan Debt to Equity Ratio (DER) berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan. Demikian pula, Profitabilitas yang diproksikan dengan Return on Assets (ROA) berpengaruh signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan.

latest.title: Exploring The Drivers of Social Media Marketing in Pakistan’s Perspective
latest.abstract: Social media marketing is essential for business influencing consumer attitudes and purchase intentions. (18 words) The study aims to examine the antecedents social media marketing activities in retail sector of Pakistan . Perceived usefulness, hedonic motivation, interactivity and perceived expectancy. Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior, it is proposed that social media usage attitude are shaped by these four factors; and attitude are associated with purchase intention. Using a structured questionnaire and five-point Likert scale will collect responses from social media users in Pakistan a cross-sectional survey design will be used. The recommended analysis will include descriptive statistics, reliability and validity checks, structural model testing, and bootstrapping to examine the mediating role of attitude. Social media platform-specific evaluations of marketing susceptibility are hypothesized to be positively influenced by consumers’ information value, enjoyment, interactive communication, and expected benefits. It seems that consumer attitudes may also link social media marketing experiences with purchase intention. As the numbers in the next analysis are simulated, they do not constitute empirical results, and the proposed relationship must be tested with real survey data. According to the study, a framework is provided for future investigations. Likewise, it can help retailers recognize features to investigate when developing consumer-oriented social media marketing strategies in Pakistan.

latest.title: Role of corporate social responsibility in brand loyalty, emotional attachment and online behavior among Generation Z consumers: a cross-national study
latest.venue: Young Consumers Insight and Ideas for Responsible Marketers
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on the triple bottom line (TBL) framework and social identity theory (SIT), this study aims to examine how Generation Z consumers’ perceptions of the economic, environmental and social dimensions of corporate social responsibility (CSR) relate to brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, and how these relationships extend to electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) and online brand-related activities across national contexts. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 815 Generation Z consumers in Chile, Germany, Austria and Greece. Structural equation modeling was used to examine relationships among the three CSR dimensions and brand loyalty, emotional brand attachment, eWOM and online brand-related activities. Multi-group analysis was conducted to assess cross-national differences. Findings Environmental and economic CSR are positively associated with brand loyalty and emotional brand attachment, whereas social CSR is negatively associated with brand loyalty and has no significant effect on emotional brand attachment. Brand loyalty positively influences eWOM, while emotional brand attachment positively influences online brand-related activities. Most structural relationships vary significantly across countries, although the relationship between emotional brand attachment and online brand-related activities remains consistent across countries. Originality/value The study advances CSR research by treating CSR as a multidimensional set of signals rather than a homogeneous construct and examining their differentiated implications for consumer–brand relationships. Integrating TBL with an identity-based perspective from SIT, it shows that different CSR dimensions may carry different relevance for Gen Z consumers, and that their effects vary across natio

latest.title: Toward Autonomous Omnichannel Architectures for AI-Driven Consumer Experiences The Agentic Mirror
INTEGRASI KINERJA ESG, STRATEGI HIJAU, DAN KEBERLANJUTAN TERHADAP NILAI PERUSAHAAN DI NEGARA BERKEMBANG: SEBUAH TINJAUAN LITERATUR SISTEMATIS
latest.abstract: This study synthesizes empirical evidence on the relationship between ESG performance, green strategy, and sustainability practices and firm value in developing countries. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, the systematic literature review examines 27 articles published between 2021 and 2026 and indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, or Sinta 1–2. The synthesis shows that the ESG firm value relationship in developing countries tends to be positive but contingent: the effect weakens or turns negative in the short term, in heavily polluting industries, and when ESG controversies occur. Green strategy improves firm performance and value with a time lag, particularly when it targets core operations and is supported by policy incentives and long-term investors. The three constructs are complementary: green innovation and sustainability reporting quality link ESG to firm value, whereas merely formal or symbolic commitments do not create value. The study proposes four integrative propositions on timing, credibility, institutional support, and complementarity, together with a future research agenda.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

The journal is highly regarded in the academic community, particularly within the fields of Business, Management, and Accounting, with a specific focus on Marketing.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Abstract Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment.
